findings_deduped.title: Green success text fails WCAG AA contrast on the light inspector background

findings_deduped.evidence: RunHistoryView.swift:81-84 renders `Label("Success", ...).font(.footnote).foregroundStyle(.green)`. SwiftUI `.green` (~#34C759 / system green) on the app's near-white inspector background (DesignColor.bgPane #f7f7f9) is roughly 1.9:1 — well under 4.5:1 for this footnote-size text.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Use a darker AA-compliant green for text (e.g. the design token DesignColor.green #249C50 is closer but still verify ~4.5:1, or `Color(nsColor:.systemGreen)` with Increase Contrast). Better: color only the icon and render the word "Success" in `.primary`/`.secondary` so the text itself always meets contrast.

findings_deduped.title: Failure message reachable only via hover tooltip (.help) — not keyboard/VoiceOver/visible
findings_deduped.rule: HIG Accessibility — never hide information behind hover-only affordances; provide a text alternative reachable without a pointer. Charter "surface the real stderr ... Fail loud."
findings_deduped.evidence: RunHistoryView.swift:85-90: failure shows `Label(code, systemImage:"xmark.octagon.fill").help(message)`. The human-readable error `message` is only exposed through `.help()`, a mouse-hover tooltip. Keyboard-only and VoiceOver users, and anyone not hovering, never see why the run failed; the code alone is shown.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Render the message as visible secondary text under the code (a `Text(message).font(.footnote).foregroundStyle(.secondary).lineLimit(2)`), and/or add `.accessibilityLabel("Failed: \(code). \(message)")` to the row so VoiceOver speaks it. Keep `.help` as an addition, not the sole channel.

findings_deduped.title: DesignTokens hardcodes accent #007aff instead of system accent
findings_deduped.rule: Charter "system accent colour (.tint(.accentColor)) ... NOT a hardcoded blue".
findings_deduped.evidence: DesignTokens.swift:9 `static let accent = Color(red: 0/255, green: 122/255, blue: 255/255) // #007aff`. The charter mandates `.tint(.accentColor)` from the asset catalogue (user's chosen Mac accent), not a fixed blue. RunHistoryView shares this token namespace (its sibling design colors DesignColor.green/red are the intended status palette).
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Remove the hardcoded DesignColor.accent; drive accent via `.tint(.accentColor)` at the app root and use system-derived colors. Status colors should use system-adaptive `Color(nsColor:.systemGreen/.systemRed)` rather than fixed sRGB.

findings_deduped.title: Algorithm picker leaks forbidden-framework jargon ("Vision Mask", "Saliency") in user-facing copy
findings_deduped.rule: Charter: "No import Vision … A test scans Sources/" and "NO aspirational labels / labels that lie about what the app is doing" — the GUI is forbidden from Vision and must not surface framework internals as if it owned them. Also HIG Typography/Writing: use plain, user-meaningful labels, not implementation jargon.
findings_deduped.evidence: Screenshot 02-demo-populated.png shows the Inspector "Algorithm" segmented control with segments "Auto | Vision Mask | Person | Saliency". Sources/Models/Config.swift:45-56 defines displayLabel "Vision Mask"/"Saliency" and helpText "VNGenerateForegroundInstanceMaskRequest", "VNGenerateObjectnessBasedSaliencyImageRequest" — Vision API names in a codebase the charter forbids from importing Vision.

Keep Picker(.segmented) stock; only change the displayLabel/helpText strings in Config.swift.

findings_deduped.title: Entire zoom/pan/floating-control interaction model has no counterpart in the SSOT (>3% drift)
findings_deduped.rule: Every Swift screen must match its HTML counterpart; drift > 3% is a release blocker (CLAUDE.md "Design reference (this is the spec)"). The SSOT dual view is a static 2-pane grid.

findings_deduped.title: Icon-only zoom buttons have no accessibilityLabel and no accessibilityIdentifier

findings_deduped.title: Post-drop summary selected but NO summary chip renders — dead state
findings_deduped.rule: Charter 'AI-driven verification': every UI state in the design must have a matching, visible Swift screen; the summary phase must show real content. SSOT drop FSM defines summary as a visible state (DropPhase.swift:27 'ingest ── scan complete ──▶ summary(s)').
findings_deduped.evidence: Screenshot: the Tweaks panel row 'Post-drop summary' shows a checkmark (active), yet the entire left content area shows only the empty 'Drop images here' drop zone + 'Try Demo' button — no green summary chip, no overlay. findings_deduped.fixSketch: Render the DropSummaryChip at window level (in BgBgOneApp.swift's `.overlay`/`.safeAreaInset` on the detail VStack) the same way DropVeil and IngestOverlay already are (BgBgOneApp.swift:173-183), so it is visible regardless of whether the file list is empty. Alternatively, have DemoPhase.summary seed a non-empty `images:` array so the Table renders and the inset shows. Either way the summary state must produce visible stock-SwiftUI content.

findings_deduped.title: Phase rows have no accessibilityIdentifier or label and undersized hit targets

findings_deduped.title: Space-bar does not toggle the Quick Look panel closed (HIG toggle contract broken)
findings_deduped.rule: macOS Quick Look HIG / Finder behaviour: pressing Space with the preview open dismisses it (Space is a toggle: open ↔ close). The standard QLPreviewPanel handles Space-to-close only when the panel holds key focus.
findings_deduped.evidence: QuickLookController.present(urls:) (QuickLookKeyResponder.swift:71-80): when the panel is already visible it calls `panel?.reloadData()` instead of closing it. The hidden KeyResponderView grabs first responder in viewDidMoveToWindow (line 37) and its keyDown maps Space (keyCode 49) to onSpace → present() (line 42). So once the panel is up, the key view (not the panel) may still receive Space and re-present/reload rather than letting QLPreviewPanel close. There is no `orderOut`/close branch anywhere.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: In present(), branch on visibility: if `panel.isVisible` call `panel.orderOut(nil)` (toggle closed) instead of `reloadData()`; only reloadData when the URL set actually changed. Let the real QLPreviewPanel own Space-to-close by not re-grabbing first responder while the panel is key (see focus-steal finding). Keep it stock — no custom dismissal UI.

findings_deduped.title: viewDidMoveToWindow unconditionally steals first responder, hijacking Table keyboard focus
findings_deduped.rule: HIG keyboard / focus: the focused control owns key events; an app must not forcibly seize first responder from the user's focused view. The Table is the Finder-style focus owner for selection, type-select, arrow navigation, Space/Return/Delete.
findings_deduped.evidence: KeyResponderView.viewDidMoveToWindow (QuickLookKeyResponder.swift:35-38) calls `window?.makeFirstResponder(self)` every time the view is attached to a window, with no guard. This hidden background view (FileListView.swift:86-92 places it via `.background(...)`) steals first responder from the SwiftUI Table, so Table's own arrow-key navigation, type-select, and click-to-focus selection compete with / are pre-empted by the responder.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Do not force first responder on attach. Either let the SwiftUI Table own focus and attach key handling via `.onKeyPress(.space/.return/.delete)` on the Table (macOS 14+ stock SwiftUI), or only become first responder when the Table is not focused. Remove the unconditional makeFirstResponder call.

findings_deduped.title: Hardcoded #007aff accent instead of system .accentColor (seed violation reachable here via tint path)
findings_deduped.rule: Charter (CLAUDE.md:28): colour MUST be the system accent via `.tint(.accentColor)`, NOT a hardcoded blue. DesignTokens.swift defines `DesignColor.accent = #007aff`. While DropVeil itself uses `.accentColor` correctly, the surrounding shipping UI (ConfigPanel/DebugOverlay visible in this same window) and the dashed border colour pipeline still depend on the hardcoded token, so the window does not honour the user's chosen Mac accent.
findings_deduped.evidence: DesignTokens.swift:9 `static let accent = Color(red: 0/255, green: 122/255, blue: 255/255) // #007aff`. The dashed veil border and chip would diverge from the OS accent if the user picks e.g. Graphite or Pink. The blue in the screenshot is fixed regardless of system accent.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Delete `DesignColor.accent`/`accentPress`/`accentSoft` and replace all usages with `Color.accentColor` / `.tint(.accentColor)`. Apply `.tint(.accentColor)` once at the window root so every accent-derived element (borders, chips, prominent buttons) inherits the system colour.

findings_deduped.title: No accessibilityIdentifier or accessibility label/role on the drop veil or its controls
findings_deduped.rule: Accessibility authority #4: every interactive/meaningful element needs an accessibilityIdentifier AND a label/role; HIG Accessibility (VoiceOver). The veil conveys critical state ('Add folder X') purely visually with no a11y annotation, and a grep of Sources/ returns zero accessibilityIdentifier/accessibilityLabel occurrences.
findings_deduped.evidence: `grep -rc accessibilityIdentifier|accessibilityLabel Sources/` returns NONE. DropOverlays.swift has no `.accessibilityElement`, `.accessibilityIdentifier`, or `.accessibilityLabel` on the veil VStack or its Texts.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Add `.accessibilityElement(children: .combine).accessibilityIdentifier("drop-veil").accessibilityLabel(Text(copy.primary + ". " + copy.subtitle))` to the card VStack, and an `.accessibilityAddTraits(.isStaticText)` / appropriate trait. Establish a project-wide identifier convention.

findings_deduped.title: Blocked-drop tint uses a hardcoded .red literal rather than a system semantic role
findings_deduped.rule: Charter: "System semantic colours (.primary/.secondary/.tertiary)" and stock-system-color mandate; HIG Color: use system colors so they adapt to appearance/accessibility settings.
findings_deduped.evidence: Sources/Views/DropOverlays.swift:10 — `let tint: Color = copy.isBlocked ? .red : .accentColor`, and the dashed border + glyph reuse this `.red`. `.red` is the raw crayon color, not the appearance-adaptive system red.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Use `Color(nsColor: .systemRed)` (appearance-adaptive) for the blocked state. The non-blocked branch is already correct with .accentColor.

findings_deduped.title: Drop target uses a centered dashed-border card, not Finder's inset rounded-rect highlight
findings_deduped.rule: Charter: "Drop affordance: the same blue rounded-rect inset highlight Finder uses when you drag a file over a folder." HIG Drag and drop: use the standard drop highlight on the destination.
findings_deduped.evidence: Sources/Views/DropOverlays.swift:36-39 — the veil draws `RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius:14).strokeBorder(tint, style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth:1.5, dash:[4]))` around a floating glyph+text card, plus a full-window tint wash (lines 12-14). Finder draws an inset solid-accent rounded highlight on the destination region itself, not a dashed badge card. (Note the SSOT styles.css:409 also specifies dashed, so design and Finder charter conflict — charter wins.)
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Replace the dashed card border with an inset solid accent highlight on the drop region: `.overlay { if targeted { RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 8).strokeBorder(Color.accentColor, lineWidth: 2).padding(2) } }` matching Finder; keep the smart copy as a smaller secondary label. Reconcile the SSOT to the same.

findings_deduped.title: Dismiss (x) button hit target is below the HIG minimum
findings_deduped.rule: HIG (Pointer/controls): provide an adequately sized hit target; a bare SF Symbol image button is well under the ~28pt comfortable click target Apple uses for controls.
findings_deduped.evidence: Sources/Views/FileListView.swift:317-321 — dismiss is `Button { … } { Image(systemName:"xmark.circle.fill") }.buttonStyle(.plain)` with no frame/contentShape, so the clickable area is just the ~16pt glyph.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Add `.frame(width: 28, height: 28).contentShape(Rectangle())` (or use `.buttonStyle(.borderless)` with padding) and an `.accessibilityLabel("Dismiss")`.

findings_deduped.title: Custom selection commands mis-grouped under the Pasteboard (Cut/Copy/Paste) semantic group
findings_deduped.rule: HIG Menus: place commands in the menu/section that matches their semantics; the Pasteboard group is reserved for clipboard actions. "Select All" belongs adjacent to clipboard items but "Select All Visible"/"Deselect All" are custom selection commands, not pasteboard operations.
findings_deduped.evidence: Sources/App/BgBgOneApp.swift:59-66 binds "Select All Visible" and "Deselect All" inside `CommandGroup(replacing: .pasteboard)`, conflating selection with the clipboard section and as a side effect erasing the real clipboard commands.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Move selection commands out of `.pasteboard`; if a stock Select All is wanted use `CommandGroup(after: .pasteboard)` to add them as a distinct section so the Edit menu reads Undo/Redo | Cut/Copy/Paste/Select All | Select All Visible/Deselect All.

findings_deduped.title: Empty-label invisible Button is keyboard-reachable but has no accessibility label/role
findings_deduped.rule: Accessibility (authority #4): every interactive element needs an accessibility label/role and must be reachable/announced; an `opacity(0)` Button with an empty title is invisible to sighted users yet present in the focus/AX tree with no name.
findings_deduped.evidence: Sources/App/BgBgOneApp.swift:116 `Button("") { isDebugOpen.toggle() }` — empty title, `.opacity(0)`, no `.accessibilityLabel`, no `.accessibilityHidden`.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Delete the hidden Button entirely (see Cmd-` finding). A keyboard command should be expressed via a real menu `Button` in `.commands` (visible, labeled), not an invisible overlay button.

findings_deduped.title: Standard Help menu removed, eliminating the system Help search and discoverability path
findings_deduped.rule: HIG Menus / The Menu Bar: macOS apps should provide a Help menu; it hosts the system-wide Help search field that surfaces every menu command by name (a primary discoverability mechanism). Removing it leaves commands like Undo/Select All Visible undiscoverable for users who rely on Help search.
findings_deduped.evidence: Sources/App/BgBgOneApp.swift:83 `CommandGroup(replacing: .help) {}` plus MenuBarPruner.swift:37-38 removes any top-level menu whose submenu becomes empty — so the Help menu disappears entirely.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Keep a minimal Help menu with at least one real item (e.g. a `Button("bgbgone Help")` opening the README/website via `NSWorkspace.shared.open`), which also restores the system Help search field. Do not `replacing: .help` with an empty closure.

findings_deduped.title: Show/Hide Inspector and Run all have no menu command or keyboard shortcut
findings_deduped.rule: HIG Menus: every important toolbar action should have a menu-bar equivalent so it is discoverable and keyboard-accessible. The Inspector toggle and the primary "Run all" action are toolbar-only.
findings_deduped.evidence: Toolbar defines "Run all"/"Stop" (Sources/App/BgBgOneApp.swift:195) and "Show/Hide Inspector" (BgBgOneApp.swift:208-212) but `BgBgOneCommands` (BgBgOneApp.swift:34-67) exposes no corresponding menu item or shortcut for either; `.sidebar` is replaced empty (line 82) so the inspector toggle has no menu path.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Add menu commands: a primary action (e.g. `CommandMenu("Process")` with "Run All" ⌘R) and "Show/Hide Inspector" ⌥⌘I via `CommandGroup(after: .sidebar)`, calling the same view-model intents the toolbar buttons use.

findings_deduped.title: "Vision Mask" label exposed in UI in a Vision-forbidden codebase
findings_deduped.rule: Charter NO FAKE UI: "Hardcode labels that lie about what the app is doing. No 'on-device · Vision' text when the app is forbidden from importing Vision." The app must not import Vision (NoVisionImportTest). Surfacing "Vision Mask" as a user-facing algorithm name implies the app runs Vision.
findings_deduped.evidence: Config.swift:46 `case .vnMask: "Vision Mask"` is the displayLabel rendered by ConfigPanel.swift:68 `Text(algo.displayLabel)`. helpText (Config.swift:53-57) further states "VNGenerateForegroundInstanceMaskRequest — macOS 14+". The Swift app is forbidden from importing Vision; this work happens inside the bundled bgbgone CLI (--type vn-mask), so the GUI presenting a "Vision" capability as its own is exactly the lying-label pattern the charter banned on 2026-05-23.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: If the Algorithm picker stays, rename the label to a CLI-honest term (e.g. "Mask" or the raw --type value "vn-mask") and drop the VNGenerate* help text from the GUI — it describes the CLI's internals, not the app's. Keep all algorithm wording as a thin passthrough of bgbgone --type vocabulary.

findings_deduped.title: Color presets from SSOT dropped; ColorPicker omits the 5 spec swatches
findings_deduped.rule: SSOT: app.jsx:362 + :403-409 specify Color mode renders 5 preset swatches (COLOR_PRESETS) plus a hex input. Config.swift:157 even keeps `colorPresets = [#ffffff,#000000,#0066cc,#f06a3a,#2da94f]` for the UI to read. The Swift surface shows none of them.
findings_deduped.evidence: ConfigPanel.swift:31 renders only a bare stock `ColorPicker("Colour", selection:)`. The design's swatch row and hex field (app.jsx:405-408) are absent, and Config.colorPresets (Config.swift:155-157, comment "Used by the UI") is never referenced in ConfigPanel. This is a layout/interaction drift > 3% for the Color sub-state.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Render the 5 presets as a row of stock `Button`s (small swatch fills) ahead of the ColorPicker, each setting config.background = .color(hex:). Keep the stock ColorPicker as the custom-color escape hatch. This satisfies the spec without custom-painting OS chrome.

findings_deduped.title: Bare checkboxes for slider-backed filters give no hint of their value range
findings_deduped.rule: HIG (macOS, Controls): a checkbox should represent a binary on/off state; settings with a magnitude (blur radius in px, desaturation amount 0–1) should reveal their adjustable control or value. The collapsed checkbox-only state hides that Blur and Desaturate carry numeric parameters.
findings_deduped.evidence: Screenshot shows 'Blur background' and 'Desaturate background' as plain checkboxes with no value affordance. Sources/Views/Settings/BackgroundFiltersForm.swift only reveals the Slider + 'NN px' / '0.NN' readout AFTER the Toggle is on (lines 33-41, 53-61). In the off state there is no indication these are graduated, not boolean, effects, and 'Grayscale background' (truly boolean) is visually indistinguishable from them.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Use a labeled control that signals the parameter even when off — e.g. keep the Toggle but always show a disabled Slider/value, or move to a LabeledContent row; alternatively group the two graduated filters separately from the boolean Grayscale so their nature reads correctly.

findings_deduped.surface: App window root (visible behind the color panel)
findings_deduped.title: No .tint(.accentColor) applied at the WindowGroup root
findings_deduped.rule: Charter line 28 explicitly requires system accent via .tint(.accentColor) on the app; HIG Color: respect the user's chosen system accent.
findings_deduped.evidence: WindowGroup("bgbgone") in /Users/arthurficial/dev/bgbgone-tree/bgbgone-app/Sources/App/BgBgOneApp.swift:18 has no .tint modifier; grep for .tint/accentColor on the app file returns only the WindowGroup line. Prominent controls currently rely on implicit default accent rather than the charter-mandated explicit tint, leaving the door open for DesignColor.accent overrides to win locally.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Add .tint(.accentColor) to the WindowGroup's root view in BgBgOneApp.swift so the whole control tree (buttons, segmented pickers, color well, table selection) is unambiguously system-accent driven.

findings_deduped.surface: Inspector / Background color well + NSColorPanel ("Colors" window)
findings_deduped.title: NSColorPanel exposes an Opacity slider the app silently discards
findings_deduped.rule: Charter NO FAKE UI / truthfulness: controls must reflect real behaviour, not offer interactions that are ignored. HIG Color: don't present an opacity control if alpha has no effect.
findings_deduped.evidence: ConfigPanel.swift:31 declares ColorPicker("Colour", selection: $colourBinding, supportsOpacity: false), and the hex is stored via new.toHex() (RGB only, ConfigPanel.swift:33). But supportsOpacity:false only ignores alpha in the binding; it does NOT hide the shared NSColorPanel's opacity UI. Screenshot 10b clearly shows an "Opacity" slider pinned at 100% in the open Colors panel. A user who drags it expects translucency; the app drops it on the floor.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: There is no SwiftUI hook to hide NSColorPanel's opacity row, so either (a) set NSColorPanel.shared.showsAlpha = false when the well is engaged, or (b) honour alpha end-to-end (toHex8 + pass --bg with alpha to bgbgone). Option (a) keeps the contract truthful with the existing RGB-only storage.

findings_deduped.surface: Inspector / Config — Mask refinement & Foreground transforms checkboxes
findings_deduped.title: Activator controls render as circular radio-style marks, not standard macOS checkbox squares
findings_deduped.rule: HIG (macOS Controls › Checkboxes): a checkbox is a square box that toggles an independent option; a circle implies a radio/single-choice control. Scale/Translate/Rotate/Flip and Soften/Threshold/Expand/Contract are independent multi-select options, so they must read as checkboxes, not radios.
findings_deduped.evidence: Cropped panel shows each option ('Soften edges (feather)', 'Threshold (cleanup fringe)', 'Expand mask', 'Contract mask', 'Scale', 'Translate', 'Rotate', 'Flip') preceded by an empty CIRCLE outline rather than a square checkbox. Source uses Toggle("Scale", isOn:) (TransformsForm.swift:29, MaskFiltersForm.swift:30) — on macOS a stock Toggle in a Form renders as a square checkbox, so the circular rendering indicates a non-stock toggle/checkbox style or a control-shape override.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Render these as plain Toggle in a Form/GroupBox so they get the system checkbox (square) appearance; remove any .toggleStyle/.controlShape that forces a circular/radio look. Multi-select independent options = checkboxes per HIG.

findings_deduped.title: 'Run History' section header present with no spec backing and ambiguous truthfulness
findings_deduped.rule: SSOT drift (>3% blocker) + charter 'No aspirational labels': every visible string must be derived from real state. 'Run History' / 'No runs yet for this file.' is not in the design spec.
findings_deduped.evidence: Screenshot bottom shows 'Run History' header and 'No runs yet for this file.' grep of design/project/*.jsx for 'Run History' / 'No runs' returns nothing — this whole footer is unspecced. If it is not wired to actual per-file run records it is an aspirational placeholder.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Either spec 'Run History' in app.jsx and back it with real RunResult records per file, or remove it. If kept, the empty-state string must derive from real (empty) state, not be a static placeholder.

findings_deduped.surface: Inspector / Advanced — full filter chain editor
findings_deduped.title: Custom ClickRowDisclosure reimplements DisclosureGroup instead of using the stock control
findings_deduped.rule: Charter: 'Standard SwiftUI primitives only — no custom-painted OS chrome … Hand-rolled … context menus' forbidden; 'SwiftUI ships all of these.' DisclosureGroup is the stock element for collapsible sections.
findings_deduped.evidence: All inspector sections (Mask refinement, Foreground transforms, Background filters, Advanced — full filter chain) are rendered by Sources/Views/Settings/ClickRowDisclosure.swift, a hand-rolled Button(.plain)+Image(systemName:chevron) reimplementation of DisclosureGroup (its own doc comment: 'DisclosureGroup drop-in'). The chevrons are visible in the screenshot. The charter says use the stock control unless it genuinely cannot do the job.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Replace ClickRowDisclosure with stock DisclosureGroup("Advanced — full filter chain", isExpanded:$isExpanded){...}. If the whole-row tap target is the only reason, that is achievable with DisclosureGroup's label and is not sufficient justification to repaint the control.

findings_deduped.surface: Inspector / Advanced chain editor — text field
findings_deduped.title: Custom red RoundedRectangle stroke overlay paints a fake error focus ring on the TextField
findings_deduped.rule: Charter: 'Hand-rolled focus rings' forbidden — use stock control validation affordances. HIG: rely on system focus ring; do not hand-paint borders that compete with it.
findings_deduped.evidence: AdvancedChainEditor.swift:36-40 wraps the .roundedBorder TextField in .overlay(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius:6).stroke(parseError==nil ? .clear : .red, lineWidth:1)). This hand-painted rectangle sits on top of the stock rounded-border field; on focus it will collide with the system focus ring, and its corner radius (6) does not match any DesignRadius token (14/8/5).
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Drop the custom overlay. Convey validation state via a stock Label/Text error message below the field (already present, lines 42-46) and let the system focus ring stand alone; do not stroke a competing rectangle.

findings_deduped.title: Dense unchecked checkbox lists give weak grouping/spacing and small hit targets
findings_deduped.rule: HIG Layout & Controls: group related controls with adequate spacing; pointer/hit targets should meet the macOS minimum (~24pt height for comfortable clicking). DesignRadius/spacing tokens (14/8/5) should be applied consistently.
findings_deduped.evidence: In the screenshot the three groups stack many checkbox rows (Soften edges, Threshold, Expand mask, Contract mask, Scale, Translate, Rotate, Flip, Grayscale, Blur, Desaturate) at tight vertical rhythm with only a small checkbox as the hit target and label-only rows; the section gaps are inconsistent with the 8/5 spacing tokens and the rows read as a cramped list rather than grouped Form sections.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Render the groups inside a stock Form with Section headers (Mask refinement / Foreground transforms / Background filters); use Toggle (not bare checkboxes) so the whole row label is the hit target, and apply consistent 8pt section spacing.

findings_deduped.title: Run History section likely off-spec (not present in SSOT)
findings_deduped.rule: SSOT drift > 3% is a blocker — the design has no per-file 'Run History' pane (app.jsx Config/StatusBar contain no such element).
findings_deduped.evidence: Bottom of the inspector shows 'Run History — No runs yet for this file.' (Sources/Views/Inspector/RunHistoryView.swift:16). There is no Run History surface anywhere in design/project/app.jsx; like the filter inspector above, it is an unspecified addition.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Add the Run History pane to the design SSOT first if it is a real feature, or remove it; keep the app and the spec in lockstep per charter §'Design reference'.

findings_deduped.title: "+ Add" toolbar label diverges from spec's "Add files…"
findings_deduped.rule: SSOT copy drift. app.jsx:286 defines the secondary toolbar button as `Add files…`.
findings_deduped.evidence: Screenshot toolbar shows a button captioned "+ Add". The SSOT (app.jsx:286) specifies "Add files…" (with the ellipsis indicating it opens a picker, per HIG).
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Rename the toolbar Button to `Text("Add files…")` (ellipsis required by HIG for actions that open a chooser). Use the system `plus` SF Symbol only if also keeping a clear text label.

findings_deduped.title: Title bar shows a "3 images" subtitle not present in the spec
findings_deduped.rule: SSOT drift / charter "inherit Apple's chrome, don't craft". The spec TitleBar (app.jsx:280-296) renders only the brand "bgbgone" with no subtitle line; the count lives in the file-list header (`files-head-title`, app.jsx:443-446).
findings_deduped.evidence: Screenshot title bar reads "bgbgone" with a smaller "3 images" line beneath it. The SSOT places the item count in the Table/file-list header, not the window title.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Either use the stock window subtitle API (`Window` `.navigationSubtitle("\(count) images")`) which renders Apple's native title/subtitle stack, or remove the subtitle and surface the count in the Table header per the SSOT. Do not hand-stack two Text views to fake a title/subtitle.

findings_deduped.title: Preview tags read "ORIGINAL" / "CUTOUT" instead of spec "Original" / "Removed"
findings_deduped.rule: SSOT copy drift. app.jsx:327,331 set dual-pane tags to "Original" and "Removed" (title case).
findings_deduped.evidence: In the screenshot the two preview panes are tagged "ORIGINAL" and "CUTOUT" (all-caps). The SSOT specifies title-case "Original" and "Removed".
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Set the tag Text to "Original"/"Removed" and let SwiftUI render system casing; if all-caps is desired use `.textCase(.uppercase)` on a stock `Text` rather than hardcoding uppercase strings, but the spec value is title-case "Removed" not "CUTOUT".

findings_deduped.title: Filter-chain field shows greyed example text resembling a placeholder/aspirational hint
findings_deduped.rule: Charter: "No placeholder art, no aspirational labels"; every string must derive from real state. A static "e.g. …" example is acceptable only as a true `TextField` prompt, not as faux content.
findings_deduped.evidence: Under "Advanced — full filter chain" the screenshot shows greyed monospace text `e.g. mask:feather=9;fg:outline=color=#fff;width=3; bg:grayscale`. It reads as canned example/placeholder copy rather than user state.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Render this as a real `TextField("mask:feather=9;…", text: $chain)` so the grey string is the system `prompt` (disappears on input) rather than baked-in label text; bind the value to actual Config state.

findings_deduped.title: Filename-pattern token pills ((name)/(ext)/(n:02)) placed in the window toolbar
findings_deduped.rule: HIG (macOS Toolbars): the toolbar holds frequent window-level commands, not field-specific input affordances. SSOT puts the {name}/{ext}/{n:02} tokens inline beside the "Name as" text field (app.jsx:383-387).
findings_deduped.evidence: Screenshot toolbar (left of the + and Run all) shows three pill controls "(name)", "(ext)", "(n:02)". These are output-naming tokens that the SSOT scopes to the Config "Name as" field, not the global toolbar.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Move the token buttons next to the naming `TextField` inside the inspector/Config (a `ControlGroup` or trailing `HStack` of small `Button`s), removing them from `ToolbarItemGroup`. Keep the toolbar to sidebar-toggle / Add / Run / inspector-toggle.

findings_deduped.title: Sidebar and inspector toggle are icon-only with no visible/aria label
findings_deduped.rule: HIG (Toolbars + Accessibility): icon-only toolbar buttons need an accessibility label and ideally a help tooltip; hit target >= 44pt advisory / >= ~28pt control min.
findings_deduped.evidence: Screenshot shows a glyph-only sidebar toggle (far left) and a glyph-only inspector toggle (far right) with no text. Without labels these are unannounced to VoiceOver.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Use `Label("Hide Sidebar", systemImage: "sidebar.left")` with `.labelStyle(.iconOnly)` and add `.help("Toggle Sidebar")`; same for the inspector toggle. SwiftUI then exposes a proper accessibility label.

findings_deduped.title: Sidebar source-list copy ("Library / All Files / Sources / bgbgone-demo") is not defined in the SSOT
findings_deduped.rule: SSOT drift / charter "no baked-in sample/demo files". The spec has no NavigationSplitView sidebar; "bgbgone-demo" reads like a baked-in demo source.
findings_deduped.evidence: Screenshot sidebar shows sections "Library > All Files" and "Sources > bgbgone-demo (3)". The design HTML/JSX defines no sidebar and no such demo entry; charter forbids baked-in demo content that users could mistake for their own.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: If a sidebar is intended, ratify it in the SSOT first and populate "Sources" only from real dropped folders (empty on first launch). Remove any literal "bgbgone-demo" seed entry. Use `List(selection:)` styled `.listStyle(.sidebar)` inside `NavigationSplitView`.

findings_deduped.title: Context-menu state has no counterpart in the design SSOT (bgbgone.html), so layout/copy/ordering are unspecified and unverifiable against spec
findings_deduped.rule: SSOT authority: design/project/bgbgone.html is the spec for layout/color/copy/interaction; any shipped UI state must have a matching HTML counterpart (drift > 3% is a release blocker). A state absent from the SSOT cannot be validated.
findings_deduped.evidence: grep of design/project/bgbgone.html for "context", "menu", "Process This Only", "Reveal", "Copy.*Path", "Remove from Queue" returns nothing — the entire 8-item context menu shown in 17-contextmenu.png exists only in Swift, with no design spec to compare ordering, grouping, copy, or separators against.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Add a context-menu state to bgbgone.html (the 8 items in their 4 groups) so the Swift menu in FileListView.swift can be diffed against the SSOT; until then the menu's copy and grouping are author-discretion, not spec-backed.

findings_deduped.title: Folder + tray glyphs are interactive buttons but render with zero affordance (look like static decoration)
findings_deduped.rule: HIG (macOS) Buttons / Toolbars: interactive controls must be visually distinguishable as actionable; an icon that can be clicked should read as a control, not as a static label. Charter 'Finder eyeball test' — Finder's status-bar items reveal their interactivity.
findings_deduped.evidence: Screenshot 20-statusbar.png shows two thin outline glyphs (folder, inbox/tray) sitting between '1 of 3 done' and the '→ ~/Pictures…' path with no border, no background, no separation — they look identical to decorative icons. Source StatusBar.swift:62-79 makes them real .buttonStyle(.borderless) Label(...).labelStyle(.iconOnly) buttons that open Finder.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Keep .borderless but make the buttons read as controls: wrap each in a fixed hit area and give the disabled source button a visibly dimmed state, or use .buttonStyle(.accessoryBar)/.plain with a .help already present plus an .onHover background. Simplest stock fix: place them in the trailing .right cluster and add a hairline separator, matching how Finder groups its status accessories.

findings_deduped.title: Icon-only status buttons fall below HIG minimum hit-target in a 28pt strip
findings_deduped.rule: HIG (macOS) Pointer/Layout — controls should provide an adequate click target (≈28x28pt min for pointer controls); a11y authority requires hit target >= HIG min.
findings_deduped.evidence: StatusBar.swift:33 sets .frame(height: 28) for the whole strip; the two .labelStyle(.iconOnly) borderless buttons (StatusBar.swift:62-79) get only intrinsic glyph size (~14-16pt) inside that 28pt strip, with horizontal spacing 14 (line 8). Screenshot shows the glyphs as small marks with no enlarged tap region.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Give each button an explicit min hit area, e.g. .frame(width: 24, height: 24) (or .contentShape(Rectangle()) over a padded label) so the clickable region meets the pointer minimum even though the glyph stays small. Keep them inside the 28pt strip.

findings_deduped.title: Dead disabled "Add files…" placeholder button in the empty-selection menu
findings_deduped.rule: Charter (CLAUDE.md lines 79-81): "No aspirational labels" / no dead UI; HIG Menus: "Hide commands that are never relevant" rather than ship a permanently-disabled no-op. A button whose closure is an empty comment is fake UI.
findings_deduped.evidence: FileListView.swift:186 `Button("Add files…", action: { /* handled via toolbar */ }).disabled(true)` — a context menu over empty space shows a single always-disabled item that does nothing.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Either wire the action to the real add-files command (fileImporter) so it works, or omit the empty-selection branch entirely so right-clicking empty space shows no menu (stock Table behavior). Do not ship a disabled placeholder.

findings_deduped.title: Design SSOT defines no context-menu spec — surface is unspecified, drift cannot be measured
findings_deduped.rule: Charter (CLAUDE.md lines 180-182): bgbgone.html "is the spec for layout, color, copy, and interaction ... drift > 3% is a release blocker." The right-click menu (8 items, copy/labels/ordering) has zero counterpart in the SSOT, so its copy and ordering are unsanctioned.

findings_deduped.title: Segmented pickers use .labelsHidden() with no accessibility label
findings_deduped.rule: HIG Accessibility / VoiceOver: every control must expose a label. SwiftUI .labelsHidden() removes the visible label AND the accessibility label unless one is re-supplied.

In the screenshot the GroupBox captions ('Background', 'Format', 'Algorithm') sit above the controls but are not programmatically associated, so a VoiceOver user lands on an unlabeled segmented control reading only 'Person, selected'.

findings_deduped.title: GroupBox + segmented-control stack drifts from the Finder 'stock app' eyeball test
findings_deduped.rule: Charter 'Finder eyeball test': should read as a stock Apple app; SSOT drift > 3% is a release blocker. HIG: macOS settings forms use leading-aligned label/field rows (Form/.formStyle(.grouped)), not stacked full-width GroupBoxes each wrapping a single segmented control.

The screenshot shows three boxed segmented rows stacked vertically with bold section titles — this reads more like a custom inspector than Finder's Get Info / System Settings grouped form. The design SSOT (design/project/bgbgone.html) is a runtime React app and could not be visually diffed against this exact state to confirm <3% drift.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Consider a single Form { Section } with .formStyle(.grouped) and trailing segmented controls, matching System Settings/Get Info row rhythm; verify against the rendered bgbgone.html inspector state before/after. If GroupBoxes are intentional, confirm spacing matches DesignRadius regular(8) and the HTML spec.

findings_deduped.title: Hand-rolled LazyVStack + manual Divider instead of stock List
findings_deduped.rule: Charter "Standard SwiftUI primitives only ... hand-rolled list separators [forbidden]. SwiftUI ships all of these"; UI feel north star: lists use real `List`, not a hand-rolled `LazyVStack`.
findings_deduped.evidence: RunHistoryView.swift:27-32 builds the history as `LazyVStack(spacing:0){ ForEach(...) { RunHistoryRow(entry:); Divider() } }`. This hand-rolls separators and row layout instead of using a stock `List`, so it loses free List behaviors (selection, keyboard focus ring, system row insets/separators, scroll).
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Replace with `List(entries.reversed()) { entry in RunHistoryRow(entry: entry) }` styled `.listStyle(.inset)` or `.plain`; let List provide separators and scrolling. Drop the manual `Divider()`.

findings_deduped.title: No accessibilityIdentifier on any row or status element
findings_deduped.rule: Accessibility authority #4 — every interactive/queryable element needs an accessibilityIdentifier (none exist) for VoiceOver + e2e testability.
findings_deduped.evidence: Entire RunHistoryView.swift (1-94) contains zero `.accessibilityIdentifier(...)`. The outcome rows (line 79-91) and the list container have no stable identifiers, so peekaboo e2e cannot target a success/failure row deterministically.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Add `.accessibilityIdentifier("runhistory.row.\(entry.id)")` on the row and `.accessibilityIdentifier("runhistory.outcome.success"/".failure")` on the outcome Label; add `.accessibilityIdentifier("runhistory.list")` on the container.

findings_deduped.title: No composed accessibility label/role on outcome rows for VoiceOver
findings_deduped.rule: HIG Accessibility — group related sub-elements into one meaningful VoiceOver utterance; status elements need a spoken label.
findings_deduped.evidence: RunHistoryRow (RunHistoryView.swift:50-75) stacks date, time, duration, outcome, filename as separate Text/Label views with no `.accessibilityElement(children:)` or `.accessibilityLabel`. VoiceOver will read five fragmented strings per row and, for failures, will not speak the tooltip-only message.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Wrap the row in `.accessibilityElement(children: .combine)` (or `.ignore` + explicit label) and provide `.accessibilityLabel` summarizing date, outcome, duration, and (for failures) the message.

findings_deduped.title: Primary action reads "Run all" instead of the charter/SSOT "Remove background from N"
findings_deduped.rule: Charter UI north star: the primary action is "the 'Remove background from N' primary action" living top-right. SSOT app.jsx primary button copy is "Remove background from N". Label must be truthful and match spec; drift > 3% blocker.
findings_deduped.evidence: Screenshot shows a borderedProminent toolbar pill labelled "Run all". design/project/app.jsx:288 renders the primary action as "Remove background from {pending}". BgBgOneApp.swift:195 hardcodes the string "Run all". "Run all" is generic engineer jargon, not the user-facing "remove background" promise.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Change the toolbar Button title to the spec copy, e.g. Button("Remove Background from \(viewModel.files.count)") and keep .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent). Toggle to "Stop" while running, as today.

findings_deduped.title: Two filled accent (borderedProminent) buttons compete as the default action in one view
findings_deduped.rule: HIG (macOS, Buttons): a window should have a single default/prominent button; the filled style signals the one most-likely action. Multiple .borderedProminent buttons on screen create competing focal points and ambiguous default.
findings_deduped.evidence: Screenshot shows BOTH the toolbar "Run all" pill AND the Inspector "Rerun This Image" pill rendered in solid accent blue at the same time (plus segmented selections also accent-filled). BgBgOneApp.swift:202 and :278 both apply .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent).
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Keep .borderedProminent only on the single primary action (the toolbar "Remove background from N"). Demote "Rerun This Image" to .buttonStyle(.bordered) so there is one unambiguous default per view.

findings_deduped.title: Color well sits flush against the panel's left edge with no visible leading label alignment
findings_deduped.rule: HIG (Layout/Forms): form rows in an inspector should be left-aligned to a consistent content margin with a leading label; a control flush to the window edge breaks the alignment grid. SSOT: inspector content must follow consistent inset (DesignRadius/padding) used by the GroupBoxes.
findings_deduped.evidence: /Users/arthurficial/dev/bgbgone-tree/bgbgone-app/build/screenshots/audit/10-config-background-color.png — the white ColorPicker well pill renders at the extreme left of the Background GroupBox content, its rounded-left edge nearly clipped by the panel edge, while the segmented control above it is inset. The `ColorPicker("Colour", ...)` in ConfigPanel.swift:31 uses no `.labelsHidden()`/Form, so under `.fixedSize` siblings the row's leading edge is inconsistent with the segmented rows.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Wrap the Background controls in a `Form`/`LabeledContent` (or align the ColorPicker with `HStack { Text("Colour"); Spacer(); ColorPicker(...).labelsHidden() }`) so the well aligns to the same leading inset as the segmented control and shows a clear leading label.

findings_deduped.title: Pane gesture region / preview panes are not keyboard reachable and expose no accessibility role
findings_deduped.rule: HIG Accessibility: all interactive controls must be keyboard reachable and expose their behavior to assistive tech. The double-click-to-reset and pinch-zoom on each pane are pointer/trackpad-only.
findings_deduped.evidence: BigDualPreview.swift:74-78 attaches `.gesture(zoomAndPanGesture)` and `.onTapGesture(count: 2)` to the pane ZStack with no `.accessibilityElement`, `.accessibilityLabel`, `.accessibilityIdentifier`, or keyboard equivalent. Zoom is reachable via the floating buttons (once labeled) but pan/reset-by-double-click are gesture-only; VoiceOver users get no pane affordance.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Mark each pane with `.accessibilityElement(children: .combine)` + `.accessibilityLabel("Original preview"/"Removed preview")` + `.accessibilityIdentifier("preview.pane.original"|"preview.pane.removed")`. Ensure the floating ±/⟲ buttons (keyboard-focusable Buttons) fully cover zoom and reset so no function is gesture-exclusive.

findings_deduped.title: Pane background and stroke use hardcoded black/secondary opacities instead of SSOT/system semantic colors
findings_deduped.rule: Charter: system semantic colors (.primary/.secondary/.tertiary) and system materials only; SSOT pane fill is var(--bg-soft) and border is var(--border). drift > 3% blocker.
findings_deduped.evidence: BigDualPreview.swift:60-63 `RoundedRectangle(...).stroke(Color.secondary.opacity(0.3), lineWidth: 1).background(RoundedRectangle(...).fill(Color.black.opacity(0.05)))`. `Color.black.opacity(0.05)` is not a system semantic color and inverts wrong in dark mode; SSOT styles.css:117 `.dual-pane{ background: var(--bg-soft) }` and uses `var(--border)` elsewhere for 1px strokes.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Use `Color(.quaternarySystemFill)` (or `.fill(.quaternary)`) for the pane fill and `.stroke(.separator, lineWidth: 1)` (or `Color(.separatorColor)`) for the border — both adapt to light/dark and match Finder's pane treatment.

findings_deduped.title: Hand-rolled splitter with manual height clamp instead of a stock split/resizable container
findings_deduped.rule: Charter: "Standard SwiftUI primitives only — no custom-painted OS chrome ... hand-rolled list separators / focus rings" forbidden; Finder uses real split views. A Rectangle + raw DragGesture + NSCursor zone re-implements OS resize chrome.
findings_deduped.evidence: PreviewSplitter.swift:11-27 — `Rectangle().fill(Color.separator).frame(height:1)` overlaid with a 6px clear DragGesture rectangle that mutates `height = max(180, min(340, next))`, plus a private NSViewRepresentable `CursorZone` adding `.resizeUpDown`. This is a custom-painted divider/resize affordance rather than a stock `Divider`/split container.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Prefer a stock `Divider()` for the visual line, and if the preview/list must be user-resizable use a real split container (`NavigationSplitView`/`HSplitView`-style or `.resizable` panel) so the OS supplies the divider, cursor, and resize behavior. Avoid the bespoke NSCursor zone unless a stock container genuinely cannot do it (document the rdar if so).

findings_deduped.title: Splitter handle has no accessibility identifier/label/role and is not keyboard adjustable
findings_deduped.rule: Charter audit rule: every interactive element needs an accessibilityIdentifier AND a label/role. HIG Accessibility: interactive controls must be reachable and described. A drag-only splitter excludes keyboard/VoiceOver users.
findings_deduped.evidence: PreviewSplitter.swift:10-27 — the draggable overlay has no `.accessibilityIdentifier`, `.accessibilityLabel`, `.accessibilityValue`, `.accessibilityAdjustableAction`, or role; it is reachable only via mouse drag.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: If kept as custom, add `.accessibilityElement()`, `.accessibilityLabel("Resize preview")`, `.accessibilityIdentifier("preview.splitter")`, and `.accessibilityAdjustableAction { dir in height ±= step }` so VoiceOver can announce and adjust it. Migrating to a stock split container removes the need entirely.

findings_deduped.title: 'Cancel scan' renders as plain secondary text, reads as a label not a control
findings_deduped.rule: HIG (Buttons / Controls): a button must look tappable and offer a clear affordance; destructive/abort actions need adequate visual weight and a hit target >= 44pt logical. A bare .plain secondary-gray string fails the affordance and discoverability test.
findings_deduped.evidence: Screenshot 08-debug-ingesting.png: 'Cancel scan' appears at the bottom-left of the card as low-contrast grey text identical in styling to the path rows above it; nothing indicates it is interactive (no underline, no bordered shape, no hover state captured). Source confirms .buttonStyle(.plain).font(.callout).foregroundStyle(.secondary).
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Give it a real control affordance: Button('Cancel scan', role:.cancel, action:onCancel).buttonStyle(.link) (or .bordered) so it reads as interactive and inherits keyboard/VoiceOver button role, and ensure the row has adequate vertical padding for a >=44pt hit target.

findings_deduped.title: Folder glyph lacks the rounded accent tile from the spec
findings_deduped.rule: SSOT .ingest-folder-icon: 38x38 rounded-8 tile filled with var(--bg-selected), accent-colored folder glyph inside. Drift > 3% is a blocker.
findings_deduped.evidence: Screenshot 08-debug-ingesting.png: the leading icon in the card is a bare blue folder glyph on the white card with no rounded background tile behind it. The spec renders a soft selected-blue rounded square containing the accent folder. Source draws only Image(systemName:'folder').foregroundStyle(.tint) with no background container.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Wrap the folder Image in a 38x38 RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius:8).fill(Color.accentColor.opacity(0.12)) tile with the glyph foregroundStyle(.tint) centered, matching .ingest-folder-icon.

findings_deduped.title: Custom MiniDebugButtonStyle repaints buttons as dark filled rectangles
findings_deduped.rule: Charter: standard SwiftUI primitives only; custom button shapes that imitate .bordered/.borderedProminent are forbidden. ButtonStyle is allowed only when stock styles genuinely don't cover the need.
findings_deduped.evidence: Screenshot 08-debug-ingesting.png: 'Reset to fresh state' and 'Mark all done' render as dark charcoal pill buttons with white text under the DEMO section. DebugOverlay.swift:225 MiniDebugButtonStyle fills RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius:7) with Color(white:0.22) and forces white text -- a hand-painted button rather than a stock style. This also produces a dark control in a light-design app, contrary to the white/light preference.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Use stock .buttonStyle(.bordered) (or .borderedProminent for primary debug actions) with .controlSize(.small) and .tint(.accentColor); remove MiniDebugButtonStyle.

findings_deduped.title: Mono status sub-line and path rows risk failing WCAG AA at small size
findings_deduped.rule: Accessibility: WCAG AA requires >=4.5:1 for normal text. The spec sets .ingest-sub to var(--fg-faint) (#8c919c ~ 3.0:1 on white) and tail rows to var(--fg-mute); the Swift port uses .secondary at .caption (12pt mono), which on the light card can fall short of 4.5:1.
findings_deduped.evidence: Screenshot 08-debug-ingesting.png: '2 images found · 1 items checked' and the two file path rows ('client-headshots/anna_v3.heic', 'client-headshots/raw/lukas_03.jpg') render in light grey small monospaced text on the near-white card, low contrast and hard to read. SSOT styles.css:496 color:var(--fg-faint); DropOverlays.swift:76/95 foregroundStyle(.secondary).
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Use .foregroundStyle(.secondary) only for the unit words and .primary (or at least .secondary at a larger size) for the numeric counts and paths; verify >=4.5:1 against the card background.

findings_deduped.title: Status line copy 'Done · 1898 ms' truthfulness needs confirmation against real state
findings_deduped.rule: Charter: 'Every number on screen comes from real state.' SSOT app.jsx uses 'Done · {ms} ms'.

Two different times and two different state labels for the same file is internally inconsistent — at least one is not derived from a single real RunResult.

findings_deduped.title: No accessibility identifiers / labels on interactive controls
findings_deduped.rule: Accessibility authority #4: every interactive element needs an accessibilityIdentifier AND a label/role; VoiceOver reachability.
findings_deduped.evidence: The audit baseline states NONE exist today. The screenshot /Users/arthurficial/dev/bgbgone-tree/bgbgone-app/build/screenshots/audit/19-quicklook.png shows many controls (Run all, Rerun This Image, Transparent/Color/Image, PNG/JPEG/HEIC/TIFF, Auto/Vision Mask/Person/Saliency, the file rows) that need identifiers/labels for VoiceOver and UI testing.

findings_deduped.title: 'Image' background segment missing the trailing ellipsis the spec uses
findings_deduped.rule: HIG: a control whose activation opens a further dialog/picker before completing should signal it with a trailing ellipsis (…). SSOT copy authority.
findings_deduped.evidence: Screenshot Background segmented control reads 'Transparent | Color | Image'. SSOT app.jsx line 400 labels the third option 'Image…' with an ellipsis, and ConfigPanel.swift line 22 hardcodes Text("Image") with no ellipsis — yet selecting it opens a fileImporter (ConfigPanel.swift backgroundCase setter sets imageImporterShown = true). Copy drift + HIG ellipsis convention violated.

findings_deduped.title: Debug overlay is custom-painted chrome, not stock SwiftUI (app-in-an-app)
findings_deduped.rule: Charter 'Standard SwiftUI primitives only — no custom-painted OS chrome'; HIG macOS uses system controls/materials. Reach for ButtonStyle only when stock styles genuinely don't cover the need.
findings_deduped.evidence: Screenshot shows the floating 'Tweaks' panel with hand-rolled dark pill buttons ('Reset to fresh state', 'Mark all done') and custom rounded container. Code: DebugOverlay.swift:225-242 MiniDebugButtonStyle paints `RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 7).fill(Color(white: 0.22))` instead of using `.bordered`/`.borderedProminent`; line 42 strokes a custom white border; the whole panel is a crafted card floating inside the real window.

findings_deduped.surface: Window / empty content area during summary
findings_deduped.title: Finder eyeball test fail: a 'summary' state that shows the first-launch empty screen is dishonest UI
findings_deduped.rule: Charter 'NO FAKE UI': every status/state must be derived from real state and visible; 'Finder eyeball test' — nothing should look like a dead or wrong state. SSOT: summary is a distinct phase from idle/empty.
findings_deduped.evidence: Screenshot shows that while the app's internal phase is `.summary` (debug checkmark on 'Post-drop summary'), the user-visible screen is byte-identical to the 'Empty — first run' state (same 'Drop images here' tray icon + 'Try Demo' button). A real Finder-like app never enters a labelled state that renders as a different state's screen.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Make the summary phase render its own visible affordance window-wide (see finding 1). If a summary genuinely has zero added images, the chip should say so (e.g. 'No usable images found · 3 skipped') rather than silently reverting to the empty drop zone.

findings_deduped.title: Download glyph is missing its circular tinted disc backplate
findings_deduped.rule: SSOT layout/visual parity, drift > 3% is a release blocker. design/project/styles.css .drop-veil-glyph specifies a 64×64 round disc (border-radius:50%, background:color-mix(in oklab, currentColor 10%, white)) framing the download icon.

Sources/Views/DropOverlays.swift:16-21 renders only Image(systemName:).font(.system(size:44)).foregroundStyle(tint) with no enclosing Circle.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Wrap the glyph Image in a Circle backplate: .frame(width:64,height:64).background(Circle().fill(Color.accentColor.opacity(0.1))) (or .tint.quaternary), matching the .drop-veil-glyph disc; keep the SF Symbol on top.

findings_deduped.title: Count in 'Add 12 images' is not emphasized (no bold accent number)
findings_deduped.rule: SSOT copy/typography spec: design/project/app.jsx:162 wraps the count as {imageCount} and styles.css:432 sets .drop-veil-primary b { font-weight:700; color:var(--accent); font-feature-settings:'tnum' }. The numeral must be bold and accent-tinted; drift > 3% is a blocker.
findings_deduped.evidence: Screenshot crop /tmp/veil-real.png: 'Add 12 images' renders as a single uniform black/.primary weight-medium string; the '12' is neither accent-blue nor bolder than the surrounding words. Sources/Views/DropOverlays.swift:22-24 renders Text(copy.primary) where copy.primary is the flat String 'Add 12 images' (Sources/Models/DragHint.swift:56), so no per-glyph styling is possible.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Build the primary as an AttributedString or concatenated Text (Text('Add ') + Text('12').bold().foregroundStyle(.tint).monospacedDigit() + Text(' images')), or change veilCopy() to return structured parts so the numeral can be emphasized like the HTML <b>.

findings_deduped.title: Missing the SSOT secondary subline "or use Add files…"
findings_deduped.rule: SSOT spec parity: the empty state has a two-line text block (primary + faint mono subline). HIG empty-state guidance: give the user a clear next action, not just a hint.
findings_deduped.evidence: FileListView.swift:144-160 emptyState has only icon + single Text + (off-spec) Try Demo button. SSOT app.jsx:455 renders a second line `or use Add files…` in `var(--fg-faint)`. The Swift empty state omits this secondary affordance entirely.

findings_deduped.title: 'Vision Mask' algorithm label references Vision in a Vision-forbidden app
findings_deduped.rule: Charter: no aspirational/untruthful labels; the app is forbidden to import Vision and must not claim Vision in the loop ('No "on-device · Vision" text when the app is forbidden from importing Vision')
findings_deduped.evidence: The Algorithm segmented row shows options 'Auto | Vision Mask | Person | Saliency'. 'Vision Mask' (and the SSOT's 'on-device · Vision' status string at app.jsx:517) names Apple's Vision framework, which Sources/ is forbidden to import (NoVisionImportTest). The visible label implies in-process Vision segmentation that the charter prohibits; algorithm names must reflect the bgbgone CLI's real flag values, not Apple-framework branding.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Rename the algorithm options to the bgbgone CLI's actual --algo values (e.g. 'Auto', 'Mask', 'Subject', 'Saliency') and drop any 'Vision' wording in both the picker and the status bar.

findings_deduped.title: Sidebar-toggle toolbar button is wrapped in a hand-drawn circular outline
findings_deduped.rule: Charter: use real NSWindow chrome / stock toolbar items, no custom-painted OS chrome; HIG Toolbars — toolbar buttons are borderless icon buttons that gain a subtle background only on hover/press
findings_deduped.evidence: Left of the 'bgbgone' title, the sidebar/panel-toggle icon sits inside a bold, fully drawn circular ring. Stock macOS toolbar buttons (e.g. Finder's sidebar toggle) are borderless SF Symbols with no persistent circular outline. The persistent ring reads as crafted chrome rather than a stock .toolbar Button.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Use a plain ToolbarItem { Button { } label: { Image(systemName: "sidebar.left") } } with no custom Circle/overlay/stroke; let the system supply hover/press affordance.

findings_deduped.title: Developer Tweaks/demo harness chrome reachable in the shipping app
findings_deduped.rule: Charter: no Stub/Mock/Fake/demo scaffolding or fake-state controls in shipping UI; first-launch/idle state must be real
findings_deduped.evidence: The overlay (opened via Cmd+`) exposes 'DROP-IN DEMO' state cycling (Idle, Empty — first run, Drag: one folder, …, Post-drop summary), a 'DEMO' group with 'Reset to fresh state' and 'Mark all done', and a 'CLI ECHO' section. These are dev-harness controls that synthesize fake app states/results — the mock-state cycling the charter bans from Sources/ shipping UI.
