findings_deduped.title: Space/Return/Delete are swallowed (not forwarded up) when selection is empty
findings_deduped.rule: HIG keyboard: unhandled key events must propagate up the responder chain (call super) so the system can provide standard feedback (e.g. beep) and so other responders/type-select can act. Silently eating keys is a dead-key defect.
findings_deduped.evidence: keyDown (QuickLookKeyResponder.swift:40-47) always consumes keyCodes 49/36/76/51/117 by calling onSpace/onReturn/onDelete and never calls super for those cases. The handlers (FileListView.swift handleQuickLook:119-129, handleOpenInDefaultApp:131-136, handleDelete:108-117) `guard !selection.isEmpty/!ids.isEmpty else { return }` — so with no selection the keystroke is consumed and discarded with no beep and no fallthrough to Table type-select.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Have the handlers return a Bool (handled?) and, when false, call `super.keyDown(with: event)` so the event propagates. Or only intercept these keyCodes when there is a non-empty selection; otherwise `super.keyDown`.

findings_deduped.title: Primary CTA lacks any prominence — grey .bordered/.small button reads as disabled/secondary
findings_deduped.rule: HIG (Buttons/macOS): the default/primary action in a view should use a prominent style (.borderedProminent) carrying the system accent so users can identify the main action; a flat grey small button has no affordance hierarchy. Charter mandates the SYSTEM accent via .tint(.accentColor) for primary affordances.
findings_deduped.evidence: The only button in the empty state is a small grey rounded rectangle ("Try Demo") with no accent fill — it looks like a disabled or tertiary control, not the inviting primary action a first-launch empty state needs. SSOT styles the primary CTA with var(--accent) fill (styles.css:660).
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Give the main empty-state action .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent) (inherits .tint(.accentColor)) and default .controlSize(.large/.regular) rather than .small, so it carries the system accent.

findings_deduped.title: Toolbar buttons rendered inside a drawn capsule/pill outline — looks crafted, not stock Finder chrome
findings_deduped.rule: Charter "Finder eyeball test" + "no custom-painted OS chrome": toolbar items must be stock Button/Menu in ToolbarItemGroup with no hand-drawn container. HIG (Toolbars/macOS): toolbar buttons are borderless/plain icons, not wrapped in a visible bordered pill.
findings_deduped.evidence: Top-right of 01-empty.png shows the + (Add) and sidebar-toggle icons enclosed together in a single rounded-rect pill with a visible grey stroke. Stock macOS toolbar items (like Finder's) are borderless icon buttons with no surrounding capsule outline. The drawn container fails the Finder eyeball test.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Use plain ToolbarItem(s)/ToolbarItemGroup with Button(systemImage:) and the default toolbar rendering; remove any custom .background/.overlay capsule or RoundedRectangle stroke wrapping the toolbar controls. Let SwiftUI's .toolbar provide the chrome.

findings_deduped.title: Sidebar-toggle button has a heavy circular/rounded outline next to the traffic lights — non-stock placement and styling
findings_deduped.rule: Charter: real NSWindow chrome, stock toolbar items, no custom-painted OS elements. HIG (Toolbars): the sidebar toggle is a borderless icon, conventionally not boxed in a circle abutting the traffic lights.
findings_deduped.evidence: Top-left of 01-empty.png shows the sidebar-toggle glyph inside a prominent rounded-square/capsule outline immediately right of the red/amber/green traffic lights, with the same drawn-border treatment as the right group. This bordered boxing reads as crafted chrome rather than a stock toolbar icon.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Place the sidebar toggle as a stock toolbar Button (or rely on NavigationSplitView's built-in toggle) with no surrounding stroked container; remove the custom border/background overlay.

findings_deduped.title: Disabled-state explanation text is buried inside an iconOnly Label (dead string)
findings_deduped.rule: NO FAKE UI / honesty: status strings must communicate real state to the user; here the explanation is rendered into a Label that is then hidden by `.iconOnly`, so the user never sees it and VoiceOver does not get it as the label either.
findings_deduped.evidence: StatusBar.swift:62 `Label(url == nil ? "Open Source Folder (no single source)" : "Open Source Folder", systemImage: "folder").labelStyle(.iconOnly)`. The conditional text is computed then discarded by `.iconOnly`; the only place the reason actually surfaces is the `.help(...)` tooltip at :67.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Drive the user-facing explanation through `.accessibilityLabel`/`.accessibilityHint` and the tooltip, not through Label text that `.iconOnly` deletes. Use a single clear `.accessibilityLabel("Open Source Folder")` plus `.accessibilityHint("No single source folder for the current view")` when disabled.

findings_deduped.title: Borderless icon buttons in a 28px strip risk sub-minimum hit targets
findings_deduped.rule: HIG Pointer/Layout: controls should provide an adequate click target; a 28px-tall footer with `.buttonStyle(.borderless)` icon-only buttons and no `.controlSize`/min frame can yield targets below the comfortable minimum and crowd the adjacent mono path.
findings_deduped.evidence: StatusBar.swift:33 `.frame(height: 28)` bounds the whole strip; the two buttons (:65, :78) are `.buttonStyle(.borderless)` icon-only with no explicit frame or `.controlSize`. Combined height budget is 28px including the 1px top separator (:36).
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Give the buttons a defined hit area, e.g. `.controlSize(.small)` and/or `.frame(width: 22, height: 22)` with `.contentShape(Rectangle())`, and verify the rendered tap region in a peekaboo run against Finder's footer controls.

findings_deduped.title: Folder buttons are absent from the design SSOT (layout drift)
findings_deduped.rule: Design SSOT: any Swift screen must match its HTML counterpart; drift > 3% is a release blocker. The spec status bar contains only the counts group and the right-aligned mono path.
findings_deduped.evidence: design/project/app.jsx:516-522 StatusBar renders `status-grp` (left) + `.right > .mono` (path) only — no Open Source / Open Output controls. StatusBar.swift:23-24 adds `openSourceFolderButton` and `openOutputFolderButton` not present in the spec.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Either update design/project/app.jsx + styles.css to include the two footer buttons (preferred — folder-open is a real, useful Finder-like affordance) so spec and app agree, or remove them from Swift. Reconcile so drift is under 3%.

findings_deduped.title: Status colors green/amber/red hardcoded instead of system semantic .green/.orange/.red
findings_deduped.rule: Charter § Colour (inherit Apple's palette); HIG (macOS) Color: use system colors (systemGreen/systemOrange/systemRed) which adapt across appearances and accessibility (increase contrast) settings.
findings_deduped.evidence: DesignTokens.swift:26-28 hardcode green=36/156/80, amber=215/145/30, red=220/56/45. These are static and won't shift under Increase Contrast or Dark Mode. (Note: DropOverlays.swift:10 already correctly uses the system `.red`, again showing inconsistency with the DesignColor ladder.)
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Replace DesignColor.green/amber/red with Color.green / Color.orange / Color.red (SwiftUI's system-backed colors). Map status enums to these directly.

findings_deduped.title: OKLCH-to-sRGB approximation comment admits unverified color drift vs SSOT (>3% blocker risk)
findings_deduped.rule: Charter § Design reference: "Any Swift screen must match its HTML counterpart pixel-for-pixel — drift > 3% is a release blocker."
findings_deduped.evidence: DesignTokens.swift:3-7 header comment: "for v0.1 we render straight sRGB approximations close enough for visual parity" and "A later pass via scripts/colors-from-css.swift can compute exact sRGB from the OKLCH literals." The SSOT styles.css:9-24 defines bg/fg/border/green/amber/red in OKLCH (e.g. --bg: oklch(99% 0.003 250), --red: oklch(55% 0.18 30)); the Swift literals are eyeballed approximations whose drift is never measured against the spec.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: If the chosen direction is to keep custom tokens, run scripts/colors-from-css.swift to compute exact sRGB from the OKLCH literals and assert <3% delta. Better: replace surface/status tokens with system semantics (above), which makes the OKLCH-parity question moot for those roles.

findings_deduped.title: DesignFont uses fixed point sizes (Font.system(size:)) instead of semantic text styles (Dynamic Type)
findings_deduped.rule: Charter § Typography: "system fonts (.system, .headline, .subheadline, .callout, .footnote) at system sizes; never a hand-rolled tracking/weight stack pretending to be SF Pro." HIG (macOS) Typography: prefer built-in semantic text styles so text scales with the user's preferred size.
findings_deduped.evidence: DesignTokens.swift:39-47 define every font as a fixed-point literal: ui=Font.system(size:13), uiSmall=Font.system(size:12.5), displayName=Font.system(size:17, weight:.medium), label=Font.system(size:12.5). None use semantic styles (.body/.headline/.callout/.footnote/.caption), so text is locked to fixed pixel sizes rather than the system text-style ladder the charter names.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Map tokens to semantic styles: ui → .body (or .callout), uiSmall/label → .footnote, displayName → .headline, cap10 → .caption2, mono → .body.monospaced(). Use .font(.headline) etc. at call sites.

findings_deduped.title: Sidebar never applies .tint(.accentColor); selection/badge color is implicit, not charter-asserted
findings_deduped.rule: Charter: 'system accent via .tint(.accentColor) (NOT hardcoded blue)' must be explicit on the surface (priority #1).
findings_deduped.evidence: Sources/Views/SourceSidebar.swift:8-35 — the List and its NavigationLinks apply .listStyle(.sidebar) and .navigationSplitViewColumnWidth but never .tint(.accentColor). There is nothing in this surface guaranteeing the charter-mandated system accent; it works only by SwiftUI default and would silently break if an ancestor sets a non-system tint.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Add .tint(.accentColor) to the List in SourceSidebar so the surface explicitly asserts the system accent for selection highlight and the SF Symbol/badge tint, satisfying the charter independent of ancestor state.

findings_deduped.title: 'Single Files' row is hidden when empty, contradicting its own documented contract
findings_deduped.rule: Internal SSOT/contract consistency + HIG sidebar stability (sidebar item presence should be predictable, not flicker in/out based on transient counts).
findings_deduped.evidence: Sources/Views/SourceSidebar.swift:19 'if singleFilesCount > 0 { ... }' hides the row when empty, but Sources/Models/Batch.swift:9-10 documents the opposite contract: 'The sidebar always renders a row for this batch even when no loose files have been dropped yet.' The code and its T13 spec comment disagree.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Pick one source of truth. If the KISS 'hide when empty' behavior is intended, update the Batch.swift:9-14 T13 comments to match. If the documented 'always render' contract holds, drop the count guard at SourceSidebar.swift:19. The implemented behavior must match the written contract.

findings_deduped.title: Sidebar rows have no right-click context menu, breaking Finder-parity charter
findings_deduped.rule: Charter: 'Finder, but for background removal' — Finder source-list rows offer a right-click context menu (Open, Reveal, Remove). HIG macOS: provide contextual menus for list/sidebar items where actions apply.
findings_deduped.evidence: Sources/Views/SourceSidebar.swift:25-30 — each per-folder batch row is a bare NavigationLink(Label) with no .contextMenu. A batch has a rootURL (Batch.swift:23) and FolderOpener exists (Sources/Services/FolderOpener.swift), so 'Open Source Folder in Finder' / 'Remove from list' are real available actions, but the sidebar exposes none of them on right-click. This is the 'Finder eyeball test' family mismatch.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Add .contextMenu to each batch row with stock Buttons: 'Open in Finder' (calls FolderOpener with batch.rootURL, disabled when nil per Single Files), 'Remove from List'. Use stock .contextMenu — no hand-rolled menu.

findings_deduped.title: Folder batch rows lack a VoiceOver accessibility label that disambiguates count vs name
findings_deduped.rule: Accessibility authority #4: every interactive element needs an accessibility label/role; HIG accessibility: badges must be conveyed to VoiceOver, not just shown visually.
findings_deduped.evidence: Sources/Views/SourceSidebar.swift:21-22 and :27-28 attach '.badge(count)' to a Label. The badge number is decorative to AX unless an explicit accessibilityLabel folds it in; a VoiceOver user hears only 'summer-shoot' or 'Single Files', not 'summer-shoot, 3 images'. No .accessibilityLabel is present on any row.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Add .accessibilityLabel("\(batch.name), \(batch.imageCount) images") to each batch row and "All Files" to the library row, so the badge count is spoken. Stock SwiftUI modifier.

findings_deduped.title: Date renders with mixed locale formatting ('7. June 2026')
findings_deduped.rule: HIG Typography/Localization & label clarity: dates should use the user's locale format consistently, not a hybrid (German ordinal-dot + English month)
findings_deduped.evidence: 21-runhistory.png shows '7. June 2026' — a trailing-dot day (German/Austrian convention) combined with the English month name 'June'. RunHistoryView.swift:53 uses `Text(entry.startedAt, style: .date)` which is locale-derived, but the rendered hybrid indicates a locale/format mismatch that reads as non-stock.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Use a single explicit Date.FormatStyle (e.g. .dateTime.day().month(.wide).year()) under one locale, or rely on a consistent system locale so the day/month/year style is internally coherent.

findings_deduped.title: Dark/black filled action buttons instead of stock button styles in a light app
findings_deduped.rule: Charter: use real .bordered/.borderedProminent styles, never custom rectangles imitating them; light-design preference. HIG: standard push buttons adopt system styling/accent.
findings_deduped.evidence: Screenshot DEMO section shows 'Reset to fresh state' and 'Mark all done' as solid near-black pill buttons — neither the grey of stock .bordered nor the accent of .borderedProminent, and clashing with the otherwise light/white UI.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Use stock Button with .buttonStyle(.bordered) (or .borderedProminent for the primary), letting the system render fill/accent. Remove any custom black background. (Best fix: these buttons are part of the demo harness and should be deleted with it.)

findings_deduped.title: Error glyph is a circle-with-X instead of the spec's circle-with-single-slash
findings_deduped.rule: SSOT drift > 3% is a release blocker. app.jsx blocked glyph = circle + ONE diagonal stroke (prohibition mark), not an X.
findings_deduped.evidence: Zoomed crop shows a red circle containing two crossing strokes (an X / xmark). The spec at /Users/arthurficial/dev/bgbgone-tree/bgbgone-app/design/project/app.jsx:186-189 draws `<circle r=17> + <path d="M11 11l22 22">` — a single diagonal slash (a 'no entry' mark), one stroke only.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Match the spec: render a circle with a single diagonal slash. In stock SwiftUI use Image(systemName: "nosign") (circle + single slash) tinted .red, rather than xmark.circle. Pick the SF Symbol that matches the spec glyph.

findings_deduped.title: Centered modal 'Nothing to add' card is a non-Finder invalid-drop affordance
findings_deduped.rule: Charter 'Finder eyeball test' + 'Drop affordance: the same blue rounded-rect inset highlight Finder uses'. Finder signals an invalid drop with the no-drop cursor badge and by NOT highlighting the target — not a centered modal card.
findings_deduped.evidence: Screenshot shows a large centered modal card (dashed red border, X glyph, headline + sub) blocking the window during a drag. Finder never presents such a card for an unusable drag; it shows the prohibition badge on the drag image and leaves the window unhighlighted. This looks 'crafted', not stock.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: For invalid drops, return [] / refuse from the .onDrop validation so the system shows the no-drop cursor, and simply do not highlight the drop target; reserve any inset highlight for valid drags. If a hint is kept, demote it to a subtle status-bar line rather than a full-window modal card. (Note: SSOT specifies this card, so resolve the charter-vs-SSOT conflict in favour of the charter, which is priority 1.)

findings_deduped.surface: Mask refinement vs Foreground transforms / Background — inconsistent row grouping
findings_deduped.title: Toggle+control rows are inconsistently wrapped: some in a VStack, expand/contract/translate/flip are bare siblings
findings_deduped.rule: HIG Layout (consistency) + Forms: related controls that form one logical row should be grouped consistently so the toggle and its dependent control read as a unit and align predictably.
findings_deduped.evidence: featherRow/thresholdRow wrap Toggle+Slider in `VStack(alignment:.leading, spacing:4)` (MaskFiltersForm.swift:29,49). But expandRow/contractRow emit a bare `Toggle` then a bare `Stepper` with no wrapping VStack (MaskFiltersForm.swift:69-75, 84-90); same pattern in TransformsForm.swift translateRow (51-63) and flipRow (92-102). They are flattened into the parent VStack(spacing:12), so the toggle and its dependent control get 12pt apart instead of the 4pt intra-pair spacing used elsewhere — visually they no longer read as one pair.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Wrap each toggle+dependent-control in `VStack(alignment:.leading, spacing:4)` exactly as featherRow does, so all rows share one grouping/spacing convention.

findings_deduped.title: Hand-rolled RoundedRectangle error ring overlaid on a .roundedBorder TextField (mismatched custom chrome)
findings_deduped.rule: Charter: standard SwiftUI primitives only, no custom-painted chrome imitating system controls; corner radius must match the real control. SSOT/HIG: error state should use the system field's own focus/validation affordance.
findings_deduped.evidence: AdvancedChainEditor.swift:33 applies `.textFieldStyle(.roundedBorder)` then :36-40 overlays a manual `RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 6).stroke(... Color.red ...)`. The hardcoded 6pt radius does not necessarily match the system rounded-border field's radius, producing a hand-painted ring around real chrome (double border on error).
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Drop the overlay; signal the error via the existing Label(err) message plus .accessibilityLabel, or use a stock container (e.g. a GroupBox/border tinted with .tint) rather than re-stroking the field. If a tint is needed use the system field's own styling, not a separately-radiused rectangle.

findings_deduped.title: Custom hand-rolled disclosure replaces stock DisclosureGroup with a manually painted chevron
findings_deduped.rule: Charter: "Hand-rolled ... list separators, hand-rolled context menus. SwiftUI ships all of these" — and stock primitives only; DisclosureGroup is the stock disclosure control.
findings_deduped.evidence: ClickRowDisclosure.swift:8-34 re-implements disclosure from Button(.plain)+Image(systemName:"chevron.down/right") with a hardcoded `.font(.system(size: 10, weight: .semibold))` chevron (:18) instead of using SwiftUI's DisclosureGroup. The file's own doc comment calls it a "DisclosureGroup drop-in". This is custom-painted OS chrome for an element SwiftUI already provides.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Replace with stock `DisclosureGroup(title, isExpanded: $isExpanded) { content }`. If full-row tappability is the genuine reason, document the platform limitation per charter and at minimum use a semantic font for the chevron, not a hardcoded 10pt size.

findings_deduped.title: Grayscale row is inconsistent with sibling rows (no disclosure-of-value parity) — acceptable but unlabeled for a11y
findings_deduped.rule: Charter authority #4: accessibility label/identifier on every interactive element.
findings_deduped.evidence: BackgroundFiltersForm.swift:22 `Toggle("Grayscale background", isOn: $config.bgGrayscale)` — a bare Toggle with no .accessibilityIdentifier (consistent with the broader finding, called out here because it is the one boolean-only control with no dependent slider to anchor an ID).
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Add .accessibilityIdentifier("bg.grayscale.toggle"). The visible title already serves as the accessibility label.

findings_deduped.title: Paired X/Y steppers in an HStack lack distinct accessibility labels and identifiers
findings_deduped.rule: HIG Steppers + Accessibility: each stepper must be independently identifiable and labeled; two adjacent steppers reading only "X: 0 px" / "Y: 0 px" visually is fine but both need IDs/labels for VoiceOver and e2e targeting.
findings_deduped.evidence: TransformsForm.swift:53-62 places two Steppers in one HStack (`Stepper("X: \(x) px", ...)` and `Stepper("Y: \(y) px", ...)`) with no .accessibilityIdentifier and no explicit .accessibilityLabel; the value is baked into the title string so it changes as the user steps, making it an unstable accessibility label.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Give each a stable .accessibilityLabel ("Translate X"/"Translate Y") and .accessibilityValue("\(x) px"), plus .accessibilityIdentifier("fg.translateX.stepper")/"...Y..."; keep the visible title as-is or move the value out of the label.

findings_deduped.title: Spec's selected-row accent text styling not reproducible / not attempted under stock Table
findings_deduped.rule: SSOT styles.css:334-335 `.file-row.selected { background: var(--bg-selected) } .file-row.selected .fr-name { color: var(--accent-press); font-weight: 600 }`; Charter: stock selection appearance via system accent
findings_deduped.evidence: The design selects a single row, tints its background with bg-selected (accent 9% mix) and bolds the name in accent-press. The Swift Table (FileListView.swift:19) uses the stock multi-select highlight (correct per charter) but the Name cell (20-28) never reflects selection, so selected rows look identical to the design only by luck of the system highlight; the spec's accent-bold name is dropped. This is acceptable under "inherit Apple's chrome," but it is undocumented drift from the SSOT.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Accept stock selection highlight as the source of truth and update the SSOT to drop the custom selected-name styling (preferred, charter-aligned), OR document the deviation. Do NOT hand-paint a selected background to mimic the HTML.

findings_deduped.title: Tappable text inside a Table cell creates an inconsistent, undiscoverable hit target
findings_deduped.rule: HIG Lists and tables / Pointer: row activation should be predictable; a single in-cell tap target that diverges from row selection is a hidden affordance. Charter: don't hand-roll interactions the Table already provides.
findings_deduped.evidence: FileListView.swift:271-277 the Cutout filename `Text(...).onTapGesture { if exists { NSWorkspace.shared.open(cutoutURL) } }`. This makes only the text glyphs (not the full cell) open the cutout, competing with the row's own click-to-select and double-click-primaryAction. Hit area is the text bounds only — far below any reasonable target and invisible to keyboard/VoiceOver. The "Open Cutout" action already exists in the context menu (203).
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Remove the onTapGesture; rely on the row's primaryAction (double-click) and the existing context-menu "Open Cutout" item, which are the discoverable, keyboard- and VoiceOver-reachable paths.

findings_deduped.title: Delete key bypasses the destructive-confirmation dialog for selections under 10 items
findings_deduped.rule: HIG Modality / destructive actions; Charter: native .confirmationDialog for destructive ops. Inconsistent guarding of a destructive keyboard path.
findings_deduped.evidence: FileListView.swift:108-117 handleDelete() only shows showDeleteConfirm when `ids.count >= 10`; for 1–9 selected files it calls `viewModel.removeFiles(ids:)` immediately with no confirm and no undo. The context-menu "Remove from Queue" (role .destructive, 234-235) likewise removes without confirmation. A stray Delete keypress silently drops queue items.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Either always route destructive removal through the .confirmationDialog, or provide undo (NSUndoManager / a toast with Undo). Don't split behavior by count without an undo affordance.

findings_deduped.title: Keyboard handling reimplemented in a hidden NSView instead of stock SwiftUI/Table keyboard support
findings_deduped.rule: Charter: "Standard SwiftUI primitives only — no custom-painted OS chrome ... hand-rolled focus rings ... SwiftUI ships all of these." HIG keyboard: respect standard table key handling.
findings_deduped.evidence: QuickLookKeyResponder.swift:28-47 is a hidden first-responder NSView that intercepts raw keyCodes (Space 49, Return 36/76, Delete 51/117). It calls `window?.makeFirstResponder(self)` in viewDidMoveToWindow (37), which can steal focus from the Table and break the Table's own type-select / arrow-key row navigation and standard focus ring. This is a hand-rolled keyboard layer over a control that already supports Space (Quick Look), Return, and selection.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Prefer SwiftUI `.onKeyPress(.space/.return/.deleteForward)` (or `.keyboardShortcut`) attached to the Table, and let the Table keep first-responder so arrow navigation and type-select work. If QLPreviewPanel control truly needs an NSResponder, scope it to forward keys without grabbing first responder away from the Table.

findings_deduped.title: Icon-only borderless dismiss button has no accessibility label
findings_deduped.rule: Audit authority #4 + HIG Accessibility: icon-only controls must expose a text label for VoiceOver. An xmark.circle.fill with `.buttonStyle(.plain)` and no label is announced as an unlabeled button.
findings_deduped.evidence: FileListView.swift:317-321 `Button(action: onDismiss) { Image(systemName: "xmark.circle.fill") ... }.buttonStyle(.plain)` — no `.accessibilityLabel`, no `.help`, no identifier.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Add `.accessibilityLabel("Dismiss")` and `.help("Dismiss")` plus `.accessibilityIdentifier("dropSummary.dismiss")`. Consider `Label("Dismiss", systemImage: "xmark.circle.fill")` with `.labelStyle(.iconOnly)` so the label travels with the control.

findings_deduped.title: ColorPicker control has no accessibilityIdentifier
findings_deduped.rule: Audit authority #4: every interactive element needs an accessibilityIdentifier. The ColorPicker is the color-modal trigger in this surface and is untargetable in e2e.
findings_deduped.evidence: ConfigPanel.swift:31 `ColorPicker("Colour", selection: $colourBinding, supportsOpacity: false)` — no `.accessibilityIdentifier`.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Add `.accessibilityIdentifier("config.background.colorPicker")`. The visible label 'Colour' supplies the a11y label; keep it.

findings_deduped.title: Two divergent file-picker mechanisms; NSOpenPanel bypasses the stock SwiftUI .fileImporter the charter prefers
findings_deduped.rule: Charter 'Sheets / dialogs: native .sheet, .alert, .fileImporter — never a custom modal' and 'STOCK SwiftUI primitives only'. SaveToRow and ConfigPanel use `.fileImporter`; addFiles() uses a raw AppKit `NSOpenPanel().runModal()`. Mixing two pickers for the same conceptual 'choose files/folder' action is inconsistent modality.
findings_deduped.evidence: BgBgOneApp.swift:237-245 addFiles() builds `NSOpenPanel()` and calls `panel.runModal()`; ConfigPanel.swift:81-85 and BgBgOneApp.swift:342 SaveToRow use `.fileImporter(...)`. Two different modal styles for picking files vs folders.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Prefer `.fileImporter(isPresented:allowedContentTypes:allowsMultipleSelection:)` for the Add Files flow too, so all pickers are the same stock SwiftUI sheet. If NSOpenPanel is retained for multi-select ergonomics, document the rdar/rationale per the charter's workaround rule.

findings_deduped.surface: Modals / Color picker entry via segmented Picker
findings_deduped.title: Selecting 'Image' in the segmented Picker silently opens a file-import modal as a side effect of a selection change
findings_deduped.rule: HIG modality: a modal should be presented in response to a clear user request, and a segmented control's selection is a state toggle, not a 'present a dialog' command. Triggering a fileImporter from the binding's setter couples selection to an unexpected modal, and if the user cancels the import the segment state and config can desync.
findings_deduped.evidence: ConfigPanel.swift:106-109 backgroundCase setter `case .image: imageImporterShown = true` — picking the 'Image' segment opens the importer; on cancel (handleImagePick only acts on .success, ConfigPanel.swift:114-118) config.background is never set to .image, so the segment shows selected-but-no-image or reverts unexpectedly.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Set the segment selection only after a successful import, or present an explicit 'Choose…' button (as the .image branch already shows at ConfigPanel.swift:42) and handle the .failure/cancel case by restoring the prior background case.

findings_deduped.title: Custom ClickRowDisclosure replaces the stock SwiftUI DisclosureGroup for collapsible sections
findings_deduped.rule: Charter: 'Standard SwiftUI primitives only — no custom-painted OS chrome. Hand-rolled context menus / disclosure machinery forbidden; SwiftUI ships all of these.' Stock disclosure is DisclosureGroup.
findings_deduped.evidence: The 'Mask refinement', 'Foreground transforms', 'Background filters', 'Advanced — full filter chain' rows with chevrons are rendered by Sources/Views/Settings/ClickRowDisclosure.swift, a 'DisclosureGroup drop-in' built from Button(.plain) + Image(systemName: chevron.down/right) + conditional content, explicitly bypassing 'DisclosureGroup internal layout machinery'. In the screenshot the chevrons and headline-weight section titles are this custom control, not a stock DisclosureGroup.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Use stock DisclosureGroup(title){...} with .disclosureGroupStyle, or if the whole-row hit target is genuinely needed, document the platform limitation; do not hand-roll the chevron+toggle. Section titles should use .headline on a real DisclosureGroup label.

findings_deduped.surface: Inspector / Config panel — Advanced filter chain
findings_deduped.title: Advanced 'full filter chain' exposes raw CLI DSL (mask:feather=8;fg:outline=...;bg:grayscale) in a code textarea — leaks the terminal the Golden Goal forbids
findings_deduped.rule: Golden Goal: 'Never touch a terminal.' Charter 'Finder eyeball test': nothing should look crafted/developer-facing. A raw mono DSL textarea is the opposite of the Finder feel and duplicates the GUI controls above it.
findings_deduped.evidence: Screenshot bottom shows 'Advanced — full filter chain' with a monospace textarea placeholder 'e.g. mask:feather=8;fg:outline=color=#fff;width=3; bg:grayscale' and footer 'Composed from GUI controls (used when text alone is empty)'. Sources/Views/Settings/AdvancedChainEditor.swift:29 hardcodes that example string. This is a power-user CLI surface inside a 'Finder for background removal'.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: If a power-user escape hatch is required, hide it behind a stock advanced toggle/menu, label it plainly, and ensure it never appears in the default Finder-like view. Confirm it is part of the SSOT before shipping; presently it is not.

findings_deduped.title: No accessibilityLabel/role on the bordered-prominent Run all/Stop button
findings_deduped.rule: HIG Accessibility: every control must expose a VoiceOver label and, for toggles, a value/state. The Run all/Stop button changes meaning by state and needs an explicit label; relying on the changing text is acceptable for the label but the toggle nature should be exposed.
findings_deduped.evidence: BgBgOneApp.swift:195-206 Button(viewModel.activeRun != nil ? "Stop" : "Run all") has only .help() (tooltip), no .accessibilityLabel/.accessibilityValue. grep for accessibilityLabel in Sources/ is empty.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Keep the text title as label, but verify VoiceOver announces state; if needed add .accessibilityLabel(viewModel.activeRun != nil ? "Stop" : "Run all"). At minimum ensure no icon-only ambiguity (this one is text, so label is fine once identifier added).

findings_deduped.title: Primary button omits the pending count the SSOT requires ("Remove background from N")
findings_deduped.rule: SSOT: the primary action surfaces the live count of files to process; the charter forbids labels that don't reflect real state but also requires fidelity to the spec's informative label.
findings_deduped.evidence: design/project/app.jsx:288 shows the count inline: Remove background from {pending} with tnum styling (styles.css:105). Swift's button (BgBgOneApp.swift:195) shows a static "Run all" with no count; the count only lives in navigationSubtitle (:145).
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Interpolate the count into the toolbar label: Text("Remove background from \(viewModel.files.count)") or the pending subset, matching the spec.

findings_deduped.title: All three toolbar items use .primaryAction, flattening importance ordering
findings_deduped.rule: HIG (macOS toolbars): order toolbar items by importance/frequency and reserve the trailing primary-action slot for the single most important action; place the inspector/sidebar toggle in its own region, not in primaryAction.
findings_deduped.evidence: BgBgOneApp.swift:186, :194, :208 all use ToolbarItem(placement: .primaryAction). Finder places its sidebar/inspector toggle separately (trailing utility), not co-mingled with the action buttons. The inspector toggle is a view-state control, not a primary action.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Move the inspector toggle to a distinct placement (e.g. ToolbarItem(placement: .automatic) trailing, or use a dedicated .navigation/.primaryAction split). Keep only Add Files… and the process button as .primaryAction so the prominent button reads as the single primary.

findings_deduped.title: Copy button gives no feedback or accessibility state on success
findings_deduped.rule: HIG Accessibility: interactive controls must convey state to VoiceOver; HIG feedback: confirm the result of an action. Copying silently leaves the user (and VoiceOver) unaware anything happened.
findings_deduped.evidence: MissingBinaryView.swift:32-36 Button("Copy") writes to NSPasteboard with no label change ('Copied'), no checkmark, no accessibilityValue/announcement.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Track a @State copied flag, swap label to 'Copied' with a brief reset, and post an .accessibilityAction / AccessibilityNotification.Announcement('Copied to clipboard'). (Moot if the brew row is removed per the lying-label finding.)

findings_deduped.title: Typography uses hand-rolled numeric point sizes instead of system text styles
findings_deduped.rule: Charter: 'system fonts (.system, .headline, .subheadline, .callout, .footnote) at system sizes; never a hand-rolled tracking/weight stack' (CLAUDE.md:27).
findings_deduped.evidence: MissingBinaryView.swift hardcodes .font(.system(size: 13)) :21, .system(size: 12.5) :28, .system(size: 11.5) :40, .system(size: 11) :52, plus DesignFont.displayName = Font.system(size: 17, weight:.medium) :17 (DesignTokens.swift:43). These fixed sizes ignore Dynamic Type / system text-style scaling.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Map to semantic styles: title -> .title2/.headline, body -> .body, brew code -> .body.monospaced(), hints -> .footnote, paths -> .caption.monospaced().

findings_deduped.title: Design SSOT draws a fake title bar with fake traffic-light dots — must NOT be ported to SwiftUI (verify the app uses real NSWindow chrome)
findings_deduped.rule: Charter "NO FAKE CHROME": "No SwiftUI Circle().fill(.red/.yellow/.green) traffic lights. No custom 44px title bar view. Use the real NSWindow chrome ... App-in-an-app is an automatic release blocker."
findings_deduped.evidence: design/project/app.jsx:282-284 renders `<div className="titlebar">` with `<span className="tl r"/><span className="tl y"/><span className="tl g"/>` and a `tb-brand` "bgbgone"; styles.css:71 `.tl { width:12px; height:12px; border-radius:50% }` and :48-59 `.window { border-radius:14px; box-shadow:--shadow-window }`. The SwiftUI side correctly does NOT reproduce these (no Circle traffic lights, no 14px window radius, no custom titlebar — grep finds none in Sources/), using WindowGroup + navigationTitle + .toolbar instead. This is the CORRECT divergence, but it is a >3% literal drift from the SSOT that must be explicitly whitelisted so a future "pixel-match" pass does not re-introduce the fake chrome.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: No code change to Sources/. Add a source-scan test asserting Sources/ contains NO `Circle().fill(.red`/`.yellow`/`.green`, no `DesignRadius.window` applied to a window-level view, and no custom titlebar VStack. Document in the design SSOT that .titlebar/.tl-dots/.window border-radius are mockup-only artifacts representing real NSWindow chrome.

findings_deduped.title: Hardcoded white opacity backgrounds and selection fill break in Dark Mode
findings_deduped.rule: Charter: use system materials / semantic colors. HIG (Color/Dark Mode): never hardcode white/black; use semantic colors and materials so surfaces adapt to appearance.
findings_deduped.evidence: Selection fill DebugOverlay.swift:88 `.fill(... Color.white.opacity(0.7) : .clear)`; field/log backgrounds DebugOverlay.swift:127 `Color.white.opacity(0.5)`, :176 `Color.white.opacity(0.5)`, :193 `Color.white.opacity(0.5)`; border overlay :42 `Color.white.opacity(0.6)`. In Dark Mode these become bright white washes over `.regularMaterial`, the opposite of system behavior.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Use `.background(.thinMaterial, in: RoundedRectangle(...))` for inset fields/log; use `.fill(Color.accentColor.opacity(0.15))` or `.selection` for the active row; drop the white stroke or use `.separator`/`Color(nsColor: .separatorColor)`. Source-scan test: ban `Color.white.opacity` in Sources/Views.

findings_deduped.title: Phase-force rows and mini buttons fall below HIG minimum hit-target height
findings_deduped.rule: HIG (Inputs / pointer targets): give controls a comfortable minimum hit area. Tap/click targets should be at least ~28pt; the phase rows here are ~20pt tall.
findings_deduped.evidence: DemoPhase rows DebugOverlay.swift:83 use only `.padding(.vertical, 4)` around `.font(.system(size: 11.5))` text (~20pt total interactive height). Mini buttons (231) and inset field/log (125,192) are fixed `height: 26`. All below the comfortable click-target floor.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Use stock controls with default `.controlSize` (which meet minimums) or raise row/button height to >=28pt (`.frame(minHeight: 28)`). Peekaboo e2e: assert clickable bounds height >= 28pt.

findings_deduped.title: Custom-painted panel chrome (RoundedRectangle frame + manual shadow) imitates an app-in-an-app floating window
findings_deduped.rule: Charter: "No floating panels-in-panels", "no custom shadow", "App-in-an-app ... is an automatic release blocker"; use real NSWindow/stock surfaces. Even the design spec's TweaksPanel marks itself `data-omelette-chrome` (host chrome), not app content.
findings_deduped.evidence: DebugOverlay.swift:41-43 `.clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 14))` + `.overlay(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 14).strokeBorder(Color.white.opacity(0.6)))` + `.shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.18), radius: 40, x: 0, y: 12)` paints a floating rounded window with a hand-rolled border and drop shadow inside the real window.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: If retained in DEBUG only, present it as a real auxiliary `Window`/`.inspector`/`.popover` (real NSWindow chrome) rather than a hand-painted floating card; drop the manual stroke + shadow. Best fix: strip from shipping per the blocker, so this chrome never reaches users.

findings_deduped.title: Zoom +/−/reset buttons below HIG minimum hit-target
findings_deduped.rule: HIG (macOS pointer/hit-target): controls should present an adequately sized hit region (≈28pt min for comfortable mouse targeting). Tiny plain-glyph buttons packed in a compact capsule are hard to hit.
findings_deduped.evidence: Bottom-right of the CUTOUT pane shows a small capsule with three magnifier/reset glyphs. Sources/Views/Preview/BigDualPreview.swift:84-105 builds them with `.buttonStyle(.plain)`, `.imageScale(.medium)`, only `.padding(.horizontal,10).padding(.vertical,6)` on the whole HStack — so each glyph's tappable area is roughly the symbol size (~16-20pt), under the comfortable minimum, and the three sit shoulder-to-shoulder.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Give each Button its own padded contentShape (e.g. `.frame(minWidth:28,minHeight:28).contentShape(Rectangle())`) or use `.controlSize(.large)` with `.buttonStyle(.borderless)`; keep the capsule but ensure each segment is independently ≥28pt.

findings_deduped.title: Panel paints its own border, shadow and white hairline rather than presenting as a stock popover/inspector
findings_deduped.rule: Charter: 'hand-rolled focus rings, hand-rolled list separators… SwiftUI ships all of these' and 'don't build a brand, inherit Apple's.' HIG (Popovers/Materials): use system popover chrome and .separator, not custom strokes.
findings_deduped.evidence: Sources/Views/DebugOverlay.swift:41-43 clips to RoundedRectangle(14) then overlays a strokeBorder(Color.white.opacity(0.6)) and a manual .shadow(black 0.18, radius 40). The header divider (:61) and section dividers (:27-33) use DesignColor.border/borderSoft hardcoded grays. In the screenshot this reads as a crafted floating card rather than a stock macOS popover/inspector.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Present the panel as a real .popover or as an Inspector column; drop the custom white-stroke overlay and manual shadow (popovers get system chrome free) and replace DesignColor.border dividers with stock Divider().

findings_deduped.title: Force-phase list is a stack of custom plain Buttons with a hand-painted selection fill instead of a stock selectable List
findings_deduped.rule: Charter 'Finder, but for background removal': single-select navigation should use real List/Table selection, not a LazyVStack of buttons with manual highlight. HIG (Lists/Selection): selected rows use system selection styling.
findings_deduped.evidence: Sources/Views/DebugOverlay.swift:66-90 builds the 'Drop-in demo' radio list as ForEach buttons (.buttonStyle(.plain)) each with a manual RoundedRectangle(4).fill(Color.white.opacity(0.7)) for the active row. Screenshot shows the selected 'Drag: folder + extras' row marked only by a faint checkmark with no system selection affordance.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Use a List(selection:) with .listStyle(.inset) or a Picker(.inline); let the system render selection highlight and the checkmark, removing the manual fill.

findings_deduped.surface: Tweaks / Debug panel — section labels & log text
findings_deduped.title: Low-contrast micro-typography (10–10.5pt uppercase mute-gray) risks failing WCAG AA
findings_deduped.rule: Accessibility authority #4 / WCAG AA: text must meet 4.5:1 (small text). HIG typography: avoid sub-11pt body text.
findings_deduped.evidence: Section labels (DebugOverlay.swift:217 font size 10, color DesignColor.fgMute = rgb(102,107,117)) and log tail (:157,:169 size 10.5, fgFaint = rgb(140,145,156)) sit on a translucent .regularMaterial. fgFaint (#8C919C) on near-white is well under 4.5:1, and 10–10.5pt is below comfortable reading size. In the screenshot the 'DROP-IN DEMO'/'DEMO' labels are faint and small.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Use .font(.caption)/.footnote with .foregroundStyle(.secondary) (system semantic color, which adapts contrast) and avoid sub-11pt; let the material+semantic color pairing guarantee AA.

findings_deduped.title: Icon-only close button hit target is below the HIG minimum
findings_deduped.rule: HIG (pointer/hit-target sizing): controls should present at least a ~28pt (ideally 44pt) hittable area; macOS minimum touch/click target.
findings_deduped.evidence: DebugOverlay.swift:52-57: the close Button wraps an Image(systemName: "xmark").font(.system(size: 11)) with .buttonStyle(.plain) and no explicit frame/padding, yielding an ~11pt glyph-sized hit area in the panel header.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Give it .frame(width: 28, height: 28) (or use a stock toolbar/borderless Button which carries adequate padding) and .contentShape(Rectangle()) so the whole frame is clickable.

findings_deduped.title: Folder name shown as plain inline text, not the monospaced chip the design specifies
findings_deduped.rule: SSOT: the folder name uses the `.hint-em` style (styles.css:434-443) — monospaced font, accent-tinted background, 1px 7px padding, 5px border-radius (a pill/chip). The Swift veil renders the name as plain body text inside the primary string. This is a visible layout/typography drift on the headline element.
findings_deduped.evidence: Screenshot shows 'Add folder client-headshots' as one continuous run of identical-weight system text with no chip around 'client-headshots'. DragHint.swift:32 builds the primary as a single String `"Add folder \(folderName)"` and DropOverlays.swift:22 renders it with one `Text` + `.font(.title3)`, so no per-token chip styling is possible.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Compose the headline from multiple Text runs and give the name a chip: a separate `Text(folderName).font(.system(.callout, design: .monospaced)).padding(.horizontal,6).padding(.vertical,1).background(.tint.opacity(0.12), in: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: DesignRadius.small)).foregroundStyle(.tint)`, concatenated with the surrounding text in an HStack. Use `DesignRadius.small` (5) to match the 5px spec.

findings_deduped.title: Glyph lacks the circular tinted backing chip from the design
findings_deduped.rule: SSOT: `.drop-veil-glyph` (styles.css:419-424) is a 64x64 circle filled with `color-mix(currentColor 10%, white)` holding the icon. The Swift version draws a bare SF Symbol with no circular backing, so the icon floats. Layout drift on a primary visual element.
findings_deduped.evidence: Screenshot shows the folder.badge.plus symbol sitting directly on the card with a faint tinted halo only, no defined 64pt circle. DropOverlays.swift:17-21 renders `Image(systemName:).font(.system(size:44)).foregroundStyle(tint)` with no `.background(Circle()...)`.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Wrap the symbol: `.frame(width:64,height:64).background(.tint.opacity(0.1), in: Circle())` before applying the foreground tint, matching the 64x64 / 10% mix spec.

findings_deduped.title: "Cancel scan" rendered as plain secondary text, not a recognizable control; also unlabeled for VoiceOver
findings_deduped.rule: HIG Buttons: a button must look tappable/actionable; Accessibility: controls need clear labels/roles. SSOT shows it as a real link/button affordance.
findings_deduped.evidence: Sources/Views/DropOverlays.swift:102-106 — `Button("Cancel scan").buttonStyle(.plain).font(.callout).foregroundStyle(.secondary)` reads as static grey caption rather than a clickable control; no accessibilityIdentifier/label.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Use `.buttonStyle(.link)` (or `.bordered`/`.borderless`) so it presents as actionable with the accent tint and pointer cursor, and add `.accessibilityIdentifier("drop.ingest.cancel")`.

findings_deduped.title: Recently-found path rows fade decoratively via opacity, hurting contrast/readability
findings_deduped.rule: a11y WCAG AA: text must meet contrast minimums; HIG: don't reduce legibility of meaningful content for decoration.
findings_deduped.evidence: Sources/Views/DropOverlays.swift:96 — `.opacity(1.0 - Double(idx)*0.18)` applied to `.font(.caption.monospaced()).foregroundStyle(.secondary)` rows; lower rows can drop to ~0.46 opacity over the material, pushing secondary text below AA contrast.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Keep full opacity (or fade only the oldest single row), or use `.foregroundStyle(.secondary)`/`.tertiary` semantic tiers instead of arbitrary opacity multipliers that compromise contrast.

findings_deduped.title: Cmd-Shift-A bound to a custom "Deselect All" command with no design-spec basis and nonstandard semantics
findings_deduped.rule: HIG Keyboards: "Define custom keyboard shortcuts for only the most common actions" and respect platform conventions. macOS has no system-standard Cmd-Shift-A; Apple's own apps vary, so assigning it to Deselect All is a nonstandard app-specific shortcut introduced without spec. Design SSOT (app.jsx:1 "fewer affordances") specifies no menu shortcuts at all for this surface.
findings_deduped.evidence: Sources/App/BgBgOneApp.swift:63-65 `Button("Deselect All")... .keyboardShortcut("a", modifiers: [.command, .shift])`. design/project/app.jsx contains only "Add files…" (line 286) and the primary action — no Undo/Redo/Select/Deselect commands or shortcuts anywhere.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Keep the Deselect All menu item for completeness but reconsider the Cmd-Shift-A shortcut; if retained, expose it visibly in the Edit menu (it already is) and document it. Acceptable to keep given Cmd-A selects, but verify it does not shadow a focused control's needs.

findings_deduped.title: Pruner deletes whole top-level menus when they become empty, reducing command discoverability
findings_deduped.rule: HIG The Menu Bar: standard menus give users a predictable place to find commands; aggressively removing top-level menus (e.g. View) departs from the "standard Apple app, like Finder" charter north star and hurts discoverability.
findings_deduped.evidence: Sources/App/MenuBarPruner.swift:35-39 iterates all top-level menus and `mainMenu.removeItem(top)` for any whose non-separator items are empty. Combined with the empty `.toolbar`/`.sidebar`/`.textEditing` replacements (BgBgOneApp.swift:79-82) this can strip View entirely, so toggling the Inspector/sidebar has no menu path (only toolbar buttons).
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Keep a minimal View menu with real items ("Show/Hide Inspector" ⌥⌘I, "Show/Hide Sidebar" ⌃⌘S) via `CommandGroup(after: .sidebar)` so the visible toolbar toggles also have discoverable, shortcut-bearing menu equivalents — matching Finder.

findings_deduped.title: Selecting Background = Image with no prior image leaves state unchanged when picker is cancelled
findings_deduped.rule: Heuristic / state-correctness: a segmented control selection should reflect the user's choice or revert cleanly. Choosing "Image" opens the importer but never commits .image until a file is picked, so cancelling the importer leaves the segmented control visually on the old segment while the user intended Image.
findings_deduped.evidence: ConfigPanel.swift:107-108 — `case .image: imageImporterShown = true` sets the flag but does NOT change config.background. backgroundCase getter (lines 93-98) derives the segment from config.background, so after a cancelled .fileImporter the segment snaps back to the previous value with no feedback.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Acceptable to keep (no half-state committed), but make it explicit: on importer cancel, no-op is fine; ensure the segmented control's bound value is computed (it is) so it visibly reverts. Optionally show a brief inline hint. Guard the revert behavior with a peekaboo e2e (open Image, press Escape, assert segment returns to Transparent).

findings_deduped.title: No explicit .tint(.accentColor) anywhere on the surface or app root
findings_deduped.rule: Charter: system accent must be applied via `.tint(.accentColor)` so controls inherit the user's chosen Mac accent. The borderedProminent Rerun button and segmented selection should visibly track the system accent.
findings_deduped.evidence: grep for `.tint`/`accentColor` in ConfigPanel.swift and BgBgOneApp.swift returns nothing. The Rerun button (BgBgOneApp.swift:278 `.buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)`) relies on the implicit default; the charter asks for the explicit `.tint(.accentColor)` mandate so the intent is encoded and can be tested.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Apply `.tint(.accentColor)` at the WindowGroup/root content view so all descendant controls (segmented selection, borderedProminent Rerun) provably follow the system accent. Add a source-scan test asserting `.tint(.accentColor)` is present and no hardcoded accent color is applied to controls.

findings_deduped.title: Background-filter section header is sentence-redundant with its checkboxes ('... background' repeated)
findings_deduped.rule: HIG (macOS, Labels/Controls): 'Avoid repeating words from a group label in each control label.' Once a section is titled 'Background filters', each control should read 'Grayscale', 'Blur', 'Desaturate' — not 'Grayscale background', 'Blur background', 'Desaturate background'.
findings_deduped.evidence: Screenshot shows section 'Background filters' with three checkboxes labelled 'Grayscale background', 'Blur background', 'Desaturate background'. Sources/Views/Settings/BackgroundFiltersForm.swift lines 22/32/52 hardcode the word 'background' into every Toggle title, duplicating the group header.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Shorten the Toggle labels to Toggle("Grayscale"), Toggle("Blur"), Toggle("Desaturate") since the enclosing 'Background filters' group already establishes the noun.

findings_deduped.surface: File list table (visible behind the color panel)
findings_deduped.title: StatusPill "Not removed" dot uses .secondary — borderline contrast on the focused-selection blue row
findings_deduped.rule: WCAG AA 1.4.11 non-text contrast (>=3:1 for meaningful graphics); HIG selection legibility.
findings_deduped.evidence: StatusPill dotColor for .raw is .secondary (SelectedMeta.swift:92). In the cropped selected row (butterfly.jpg) the status dot renders as a pale grey disc on the saturated system-accent blue selection background, where .secondary grey approaches the 3:1 floor. On unselected white rows it is fine; on the focused blue row it is washed out.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: On the selected/focused row, status glyphs in a Table should use .foregroundStyle(.primary) or rely on the system's selection-foreground (Table normally inverts row content to white when focused); verify the dot inherits the selection foreground rather than a fixed .secondary, or switch the .raw dot to a system semantic that flips under selection.

findings_deduped.surface: Inspector / Advanced chain editor — placeholder vs example mismatch
findings_deduped.title: Placeholder syntax in code uses ':' but the audited state caption uses ';' — example is internally inconsistent
findings_deduped.rule: Charter: 'No aspirational labels … Every status string must be derived from real state' / labels must be truthful and consistent. SSOT: copy must be exact.
findings_deduped.evidence: The audited state describes the placeholder as 'mask:feather=8;fg:outline=color=#fff;width=3; bg:grayscale' (semicolon between color and width), while the source placeholder in AdvancedChainEditor.swift:29 is 'mask:feather=8;fg:outline=color=#fff:width=3;bg:grayscale' (colon between color and width). A power-user example chain that doesn't match the real DSL separator misteaches the exact syntax the field validates against.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Make the visible placeholder exactly equal to a string that FilterChainParser.parse accepts, and keep the audit caption in sync; add a test asserting the placeholder example parses without error.

findings_deduped.title: Top menu item "Process This Only" uses a magic-wand-and-sparkles glyph that implies AI/magic processing
findings_deduped.rule: Charter "NO FAKE UI": no aspirational labels/art; the app is a thin GUI over the bgbgone CLI and must not imply on-device AI magic. HIG menus: menu-item icons should describe the action literally, not decoratively.
findings_deduped.evidence: In /tmp/ctx5.png the first menu item reads "Process This Only" with a leading SF Symbol that is a wand with sparkles (FileListView.swift:195 uses systemImage: "wand.and.stars"). The sparkle-wand is the system's "AI/magic" glyph, connoting AI processing that the charter explicitly forbids the app from implying.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Swap the icon to a neutral, literal action glyph for stock SwiftUI, e.g. Button("Process This Only", systemImage: "play.fill") or "sparkle"-free "scissors"/"wand.and.rays"-free choice like "play.circle"; keep it a plain stock Button in the .contextMenu.

findings_deduped.title: "Remove from Queue" destructive item is not visually distinguished (renders in default black text)
findings_deduped.rule: HIG (menus): destructive actions should be clearly distinguishable. Charter mandates stock SwiftUI roles. SwiftUI provides role: .destructive specifically to differentiate removal actions.
findings_deduped.evidence: In /tmp/ctx3.png the last item "Remove from Queue" (trash glyph) appears in the same black weight/color as every other item, giving the queue-removal no visual destructive affordance versus benign items like "Copy Cutout Path". (Code at FileListView.swift:234-235 does set role: .destructive, but AppKit's NSMenu rendering of a SwiftUI context menu does not colorize it, so the destructive intent is invisible to the user.)
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Keep role: .destructive (correct stock idiom). If stronger differentiation is wanted within stock constraints, this is the platform's own behavior and acceptable; otherwise no further custom coloring should be added (custom red text would violate the no-custom-chrome rule). Treat as platform-limited — document, do not hand-paint.

findings_deduped.title: Drift from SSOT: design status bar has no folder/tray buttons (extra controls added in Swift)
findings_deduped.rule: SSOT design/project/app.jsx StatusBar is the spec; drift > 3% is a release blocker. The Swift footer adds two controls the spec does not contain.
findings_deduped.evidence: app.jsx:516-523 StatusBar renders only the count group and the trailing mono path (`→ {cfg.outDir}/{samplePreview}.{cfg.format}`) — no folder/tray buttons. Screenshot 20-statusbar.png and StatusBar.swift:23-24,57-80 add openSourceFolderButton + openOutputFolderButton between the count and the path. The visible footer therefore diverges from the spec layout.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Either update the SSOT (app.jsx/styles.css) to include the two Finder-style accessory buttons so spec and app agree, or remove them from StatusBar.swift. Given the 'Finder footer' intent, updating the spec is the better path — but the drift must be reconciled, not left.

findings_deduped.title: Background/border drift: spec uses solid bg-pane + border-soft hairline; Swift uses .regularMaterial + .separator
findings_deduped.rule: SSOT styles.css:663-669 specifies the footer surface (background: var(--bg-pane); border-top: 1px solid var(--border-soft)); drift > 3% is a blocker. Charter, however, prefers system materials.
findings_deduped.evidence: styles.css:663-669 sets `background: var(--bg-pane)` and `border-top: 1px solid var(--border-soft)`. StatusBar.swift:34-37 uses `.background(.regularMaterial)` with a `.separator` top rectangle. Screenshot shows a flat near-white strip — visually close to bg-pane, so the deviation is subtle, but it is a spec/impl mismatch on surface treatment.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: This is the rare case where charter (use system materials) and SSOT (solid pane) conflict. Resolve by updating the SSOT to call for a translucent material footer (matching Finder), keeping the Swift `.regularMaterial` + `.separator` which is the more correct stock-Apple choice. Document the reconciliation so the 3% gate is satisfied intentionally.

findings_deduped.title: Inconsistent ellipsis usage: disabled "Add files…" has an ellipsis but no dialog-opening item among the real actions
findings_deduped.rule: HIG Menus: "Use an ellipsis when a menu command opens a window/dialog or requires additional information." Ellipsis must signal a follow-up UI; here it is on a dead button while genuinely dialog-opening behavior (Remove confirmation) carries no ellipsis.
findings_deduped.evidence: FileListView.swift:186 "Add files…" (ellipsis, but disabled no-op). FileRowActions.swift:78 "Remove from Queue" / "Remove N from Queue" has no ellipsis even though the keyboard equivalent opens a confirmationDialog at >=10.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: If Remove is routed through the confirmation dialog (see destructive finding), give it an ellipsis: "Remove from Queue…". Drop the ellipsis from "Add files" unless it actually opens a fileImporter dialog (it should, per the previous finding).

findings_deduped.title: "Reveal Cutout" / "Open Cutout" / "Copy Cutout Path" become silently disabled with no explanation when no cutout exists
findings_deduped.rule: HIG Menus: disabled items should be understandable; for first-time users a row that has not been processed shows three greyed cutout actions with no hint why. Combined with the no-identifier issue this is an unlabeled disabled state.
findings_deduped.evidence: FileRowActions.swift:46-51,58-63,71-75 set isEnabled to cutoutsAllExist; FileListView.swift:222 `.disabled(!action.isEnabled)`. A freshly-dropped, unprocessed image yields three disabled cutout entries with no accessibilityHint/help text.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Add `.help("No cutout yet — process this image first")` (NSMenuItem toolTip) and an accessibilityHint to the cutout actions when disabled, or hide cutout actions entirely until a cutout exists per HIG's "hide never-relevant commands" guidance.

findings_deduped.title: Status redundancy: 'Not removed' shown twice for the same file

findings_deduped.title: Token chips {name}/{ext}/{n:02} are bordered Buttons — verify hit target meets HIG minimum

findings_deduped.title: Surface has no counterpart in the design SSOT — drift unverifiable

findings_deduped.title: Possible double-reversal: store doc says newest-first, view reverses again

findings_deduped.title: "Run History" header shown but empty-state copy is bland and low-contrast
findings_deduped.rule: HIG (Empty states / Layout): empty sections should give a clear, legible explanation; secondary text must still meet WCAG AA contrast. "Finder eyeball test" — stock apps phrase empty states helpfully.
findings_deduped.evidence: Screenshot shows a "Run History" section header at the bottom of the Inspector followed by faint "No runs yet for this file." rendered in very light tertiary-style grey that is hard to read against the panel background.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Use ContentUnavailableView (or .foregroundStyle(.secondary) rather than tertiary) for the empty Run History so the message meets AA contrast and reads as a deliberate stock empty state.

findings_deduped.title: "Not removed" status uses .secondary grey — ambiguous between disabled and actionable
findings_deduped.rule: HIG (Color / status): status indicators should be distinguishable and not read as disabled; the dot+label pattern must clearly communicate the actionable "needs processing" state.
findings_deduped.evidence: SelectedMeta.swift:82,90-91 maps .raw to label "Not removed" with a .secondary dot and .secondary text; the screenshot shows three rows each with a muted grey "Not removed" pill that reads as inactive/disabled rather than "ready to process".

findings_deduped.title: Mixed spelling: segment label "Color" vs row label "Colour"
findings_deduped.rule: HIG (Writing/labels) + charter "label clarity & truthfulness": copy must be internally consistent. Charter/code already uses British "Colour" for the row label.

findings_deduped.title: Floating ±/⟲ control glyph for zoom-in differs from spec intent and capsule chrome is unspecced
findings_deduped.rule: SSOT drift: the floating zoom capsule (and its SF Symbols / thinMaterial Capsule + .separator overlay) has no entry in styles.css/app.jsx for the dual view; drift > 3% blocker.
findings_deduped.evidence: BigDualPreview.swift:84-106 zoomControls render a `.thinMaterial` Capsule with `minus.magnifyingglass`/`plus.magnifyingglass`/`arrow.counterclockwise` and Divider separators. No `.dual` zoom control class exists in styles.css; the SSOT dual view ships no overlaid controls at all.

findings_deduped.title: Corner-label capsule re-styles the pane tag; SSOT tag is plain faint uppercase text with no material chip
findings_deduped.rule: SSOT spec for `.dual-tag` is plain text (no background chip); drift > 3% blocker. Charter: don't invent chrome the spec doesn't have.

SSOT styles.css:123-130 `.dual-tag` is `position:absolute; color: var(--fg-faint); letter-spacing:0.14em; text-transform:uppercase` with NO background, NO capsule. Position also differs: SSOT left/top 14px; Swift uses .padding(8) inside topLeading.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Render the tag as plain `Text(...).font(.caption2).foregroundStyle(.secondary).textCase(.uppercase).tracking(...)` at 14pt-equivalent inset, dropping the thinMaterial Capsule, to match `.dual-tag`. Or add the chip to the SSOT if the chip is the desired direction.

findings_deduped.title: Section labels use manual tracking and hand-rolled white-opacity selection fills
findings_deduped.rule: Charter: system fonts and system semantic colors; no custom-painted chrome. SectionLabel applies .tracking(0.6) and the active phase row paints Color.white.opacity(0.7) as a selection chip instead of a stock selection/material.
findings_deduped.evidence: DebugOverlay.swift:218 .tracking(0.06*10) on uppercased section labels ('DROP-IN DEMO','DEMO','CLI ECHO' visible in screenshot) and :88 RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius:4).fill(Color.white.opacity(0.7)) for the active row behind 'Ingesting folder'. These are bespoke paint, not stock list selection.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Drop manual tracking (use .font(.caption.smallCaps()) or a plain .footnote secondary label); render the active row with a stock selection (e.g. List with selection, or .background(.selection)) instead of a white-opacity rectangle.

findings_deduped.title: '1 items checked' has an ungrammatical singular/plural mismatch
findings_deduped.rule: Charter + HIG (label clarity & truthfulness): labels must read correctly; '1 items' is grammatically wrong for a count of one.
findings_deduped.evidence: Screenshot 08-debug-ingesting.png subtitle reads '2 images found · 1 items checked'. DropOverlays.swift:72-73 unconditionally appends 'items checked' after the count. Note the spec's seeded demo also feeds a single scanned item, so this surfaces in real first-scan states too.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Pluralize via inflection: Text('^[\(state.scannedCount) item](inflect: true) checked') and likewise for 'images found', so '1 item checked' / '2 items checked' render correctly.

findings_deduped.title: Status column header truncated to 'Size' / no visible sort affordance
findings_deduped.rule: HIG (macOS Tables) — column headers should be legible and, for a Finder-like Table, sortable with a visible sort indicator. Charter: 'real Table (column headers, sortable)'.
findings_deduped.evidence: In /Users/arthurficial/dev/bgbgone-tree/bgbgone-app/build/screenshots/audit/19-quicklook.png the table shows 'Name', 'Status', and a third header clipped to 'Size' at the right edge with no sort chevrons on any column, so the Finder-equivalent sortable-header behaviour is not evident.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Use Table with TableColumn(value:) sort comparators so SwiftUI renders the native sort chevron; ensure the Size column has enough width or is right-aligned so its header is not clipped.

findings_deduped.title: Uneven segment widths with visible inner pipe dividers ('HEIC | TIFF' crammed)
findings_deduped.rule: HIG Controls/Layout: segmented controls should read as evenly grouped; cramped unequal segments hurt hit-target consistency and look non-stock.
findings_deduped.evidence: In the zoomed crop, the Format control shows 'PNG' and the selected 'JPEG' as wide pills while 'HEIC' and 'TIFF' are squeezed together with a literal pipe divider ('HEIC | TIFF'); Background shows 'Color | Image' similarly crammed. This is caused by .fixedSize() on the .segmented Picker (ConfigPanel.swift lines 26,57,73) letting segments size to content and leaving trailing dead space, so the narrow segments give smaller pointer hit targets than the wide ones.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Drop .fixedSize() and let the segmented Picker fill its row (or wrap each in equal-width segments) so all segments are evenly sized and meet a consistent hit target; align width with the SSOT grid column.

findings_deduped.title: Primary label font size/style drifts from spec (.title3 vs 18px display medium)
findings_deduped.rule: SSOT typography: styles.css:426-429 .drop-veil-primary is font:500 18px/1.25 var(--font-display) with letter-spacing -0.01em and color var(--fg). Charter also mandates system fonts only.
findings_deduped.evidence: Sources/Views/DropOverlays.swift:23 uses .font(.title3.weight(.medium)). .title3 on macOS is ~15pt, not the 18px the spec calls for, so the headline reads smaller/lighter than the design. Screenshot /tmp/veil-real.png shows a relatively modest headline weight under a large icon.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Use .font(.system(size:18, weight:.medium)) (system font, matches 18px/500) or .title2 to better hit the spec's 18px display size; keep .foregroundStyle(.primary).

findings_deduped.title: Icon glyph drifts from SSOT: SF Symbol tray.and.arrow.down vs spec custom 'drop' (downward-arrow-into-folder) glyph
findings_deduped.rule: SSOT spec parity for the empty-state icon. app.jsx:453 uses Icon name="drop" (a folder-with-down-arrow path, app.jsx:27); the Swift code substitutes a different SF Symbol (a tray).
findings_deduped.evidence: FileListView.swift:146 `Image(systemName: "tray.and.arrow.down")`. SSOT app.jsx:453 `<Icon name="drop" size={48}/>` whose path (app.jsx:27-35) draws a folder outline with a downward arrow — semantically "drop into folder", not a tray. Stock-SwiftUI nearest match would be e.g. `square.and.arrow.down` or `arrow.down.doc`.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Pick the SF Symbol whose silhouette matches the spec's folder+down-arrow (e.g. `arrow.down.doc` or `folder` with a download connotation). Keep it a stock SF Symbol (no custom path drawing — that would itself breach 'no custom-painted chrome').

findings_deduped.title: Empty-state typography uses .title2 / fixed sizes rather than the SSOT display font, and DesignFont hardcodes non-Dynamic-Type sizes
findings_deduped.rule: Charter typography rule: system fonts at system sizes. SSOT app.jsx:454 sets the primary line to 500 weight 14px display font; the Swift uses .title2 (~17pt). Charter also forbids a hand-rolled weight/size stack.
findings_deduped.evidence: FileListView.swift:150 `.font(.title2)` for "Drop images here" vs SSOT's 14px/medium display line (app.jsx:454). The icon uses `.font(.system(size: 56, weight: .ultraLight))` (FileListView.swift:147) — a fixed point size that won't scale with Dynamic Type. DesignFont (DesignTokens.swift:38-48) is a hand-rolled fixed-size stack (13/12.5/17px) the charter warns against.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Use a semantic text style (e.g. `.headline` or `.title3`) so it tracks Dynamic Type, and size the SF Symbol via `.imageScale`/`.font(.largeTitle)` rather than a hardcoded 56pt. Align weight/size to the SSOT display line within stock styles rather than absolute px.

findings_deduped.title: QuickLookURLs doc-comment lies about selection behaviour (original + cutout) vs. code (one URL)
findings_deduped.rule: Charter NO FAKE / honesty: comments and labels must reflect real behaviour; aspirational/contradictory documentation is forbidden because it misleads maintainers about what the Quick Look panel shows.
findings_deduped.evidence: QuickLookURLs.swift:4-7 header says "include the original; if the file has a .done state and the cutout exists on disk, also include the cutout (original first, then cutout)" but the implementation (lines 20-25, plus the inline comment at 17-19) returns exactly one URL per file: cutout-if-exists else original. The two comments contradict each other and the first describes behaviour the code does not perform.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Delete the stale top doc-comment paragraph (lines 4-7's 'also include the cutout / original first, then cutout' claim) so the file documents the actual one-URL-per-file rule. No code change needed.

findings_deduped.title: Layout-dependent hardcoded keyCodes for Return/Delete/Space (magic numbers, no symbolic mapping)
findings_deduped.rule: HIG keyboard / robustness heuristic: key handling should use stable, documented key constants; raw virtual keyCodes are positional and fragile, and obscure intent for the Quick Look trigger path.
findings_deduped.evidence: keyDown (QuickLookKeyResponder.swift:41-44) switches on raw `event.keyCode` literals 49 (Space), 36/76 (Return/Enter), 51/117 (Delete/Fwd-Delete) with only trailing comments. No use of `.charactersIgnoringModifiers` for Space/Return or symbolic constants; positional keyCodes can mis-map on non-standard layouts.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Prefer SwiftUI `.onKeyPress(.space)`, `.onKeyPress(.return)`, `.onKeyPress(.delete)` on the Table (stock macOS 14+), or match on `event.charactersIgnoringModifiers`/`NSDeleteCharacter` constants instead of raw keyCodes.

findings_deduped.title: Try Demo hit target below HIG minimum due to .controlSize(.small)
findings_deduped.rule: HIG (pointer/hit targets) & accessibility: interactive controls should meet the platform minimum hit area; a .small control shrinks the button well under a comfortable target for the sole action on the screen.
findings_deduped.evidence: FileListView.swift:155 sets .controlSize(.small) on the only empty-state button. In the screenshot the button is a compact pill clearly shorter than a standard macOS push button, making the primary first-launch action smaller than necessary.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Drop .controlSize(.small) (use default/.regular or .large) for the primary empty-state CTA so it meets the standard control height.

findings_deduped.title: Mono path preview font diverges from SSOT size (caption vs 11.5px)
findings_deduped.rule: Design SSOT typography: the status strip is `font: 11.5px/1 var(--font-ui)` with the `.mono` path in `var(--font-mono)`; Swift uses `.footnote` (~13pt) for the strip and `.caption.monospaced()` (~12pt) for the path.
findings_deduped.evidence: styles.css:668 `font: 11.5px/1 var(--font-ui)` for `.statusbar`; StatusBar.swift:30 `.font(.footnote)` and :26 `.font(.caption.monospaced())`. Sizes differ from the 11.5px spec. (Note: charter mandates system text-style fonts over fixed sizes, so `.footnote`/`.caption` are charter-correct — the drift is the SSOT's fixed px, which should be brought to a system text style.)
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Keep system text styles in Swift (charter-correct) and update the SSOT to express the footer in matching system-style sizes (footnote/caption) so the two agree, rather than hardcoding 11.5px.

findings_deduped.title: Error-count color uses .red rather than a contrast-checked semantic role
findings_deduped.rule: WCAG AA contrast + HIG color: status text on `.regularMaterial` must meet AA; plain `.red` on a translucent material can fall below 4.5:1 and is not the dynamic system semantic for destructive/error text.
findings_deduped.evidence: StatusBar.swift:15 `Text("\(errorCount)").bold().foregroundStyle(.red)` over `.background(.regularMaterial)` (:34). No contrast verification; `.red` is a fixed hue, not a vibrancy-aware semantic.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Use a semantic/vibrancy-aware treatment (e.g. `.foregroundStyle(.red)` is acceptable but verify AA on `.regularMaterial`, or pair with `.bold()` + adequate size). Add a peekaboo screenshot contrast check of the failed-count state against AA.

findings_deduped.title: Color(hex:) initializer silently returns .clear on bad input (silent failure)
findings_deduped.rule: Charter § NO FALLBACKS: "Fail loud." / "Add fallbacks that mask failure" is forbidden.
findings_deduped.evidence: DesignTokens.swift:53-69 `init(hex:)` returns `self = .clear` on any malformed input (line 62-63), justified by a comment that the GUI hex picker "should validate before we ever reach this path." A bad hex produces an invisible (clear) color rather than a visible/loud failure, masking the bug.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Make the failure visible in debug (assertionFailure("invalid hex \(hex)")) or return a high-visibility sentinel (.red) in DEBUG; in release keep .clear only if call sites are provably validated. Better: have the hex picker hand over a parsed Color so this lenient initializer is unnecessary.

findings_deduped.title: Custom DesignRadius corner values instead of system control shapes
findings_deduped.rule: Charter § Standard SwiftUI primitives only: use stock control styles/shapes rather than re-deriving OS metrics; HIG layout: adopt standard control corner radii via system controls.
findings_deduped.evidence: DesignTokens.swift:33-35 hardcode window=14, regular=8, small=5 corner radii to mirror the HTML mock (styles.css:31-33). For a real NSWindow the title-bar/window radius is owned by AppKit, so DesignRadius.window=14 is a custom metric for chrome the OS already draws; using it on a hand-built container risks the "custom window frame" prohibition.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Remove DesignRadius.window — let the real NSWindow own its corner radius. Keep regular/small only for in-content cards, or replace with stock container shapes (RoundedRectangle defaults / .background(in: .rect(cornerRadius:)) tuned to match standard controls).

findings_deduped.title: Section header copy ('Library' / 'Sources') is not specced in the canonical SSOT
findings_deduped.rule: SSOT authority #3 governs copy; charter forbids 'aspirational labels' / requires copy derived from spec.
findings_deduped.evidence: Sources/Views/SourceSidebar.swift:10 Section("Library") and :16 Section("Sources"). These exact strings appear only in the abandoned mockup design/mockups/v0.3-power-user.html:301 ('Library') and :304 ('Sources'), not in design/project/bgbgone.html (which has no sidebar at all). The header copy is therefore unspecced against the canonical SSOT.

findings_deduped.title: Sidebar minimum width 180pt is below the comfortable macOS source-list minimum and risks badge/label truncation
findings_deduped.rule: HIG macOS sidebars / layout: source lists should remain legible at their minimum width; folder names + trailing count badge must not clip.
findings_deduped.evidence: Sources/Views/SourceSidebar.swift:34 '.navigationSplitViewColumnWidth(min: 180, ideal: 220, max: 320)'. At 180pt, a long batch name (Batch.swift:18 notes names like 'product-archive/2025-q2') plus the trailing .badge will truncate the label heavily, since the badge reserves trailing width. Finder's sidebar minimum is wider.
