findings_deduped.title: Ad hoc spacing/padding not aligned to the DesignRadius/spacing scale
findings_deduped.rule: Design SSOT/consistency: spacing and radii should follow the token scale (DesignRadius 14/8/5); arbitrary values cause >3% drift
findings_deduped.evidence: RunHistoryView.swift uses VStack(spacing:8), row VStack(spacing:2), .padding(.vertical,6), header .padding(.top,10)/.horizontal,12 — none of these derive from the DesignRadius/token scale, and there is no SSOT entry to validate against. Visually the entry in 21-runhistory.png sits tight against the section header with uneven vertical rhythm.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Adopt stock List default insets (see List fix) or pull spacing constants from the token scale so the rhythm matches the rest of the inspector.

findings_deduped.title: Glyph is missing its soft tinted circular disc background
findings_deduped.rule: SSOT drift > 3% is a release blocker. styles.css .drop-veil-glyph is a 64px circle filled with color-mix(currentColor 10%, white) behind the icon.
findings_deduped.evidence: Zoomed crop shows the red circle-X floating directly on the white/grey card with no tinted disc behind it. Spec /Users/arthurficial/dev/bgbgone-tree/bgbgone-app/design/project/styles.css:419-424 specifies a 64px round chip filled ~10% red behind the glyph.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Wrap the SF Symbol in a Circle().fill(Color.red.opacity(0.1)) of ~64pt and center the symbol, matching the spec's tinted glyph chip.

findings_deduped.title: Segmented Picker carries a redundant visible "Direction" label under the "Flip" toggle
findings_deduped.rule: HIG Pickers/Labels: avoid redundant labeling; a segmented control whose meaning is already established by the section toggle should not repeat a separate text label that competes with it.
findings_deduped.evidence: TransformsForm.swift:92 `Toggle("Flip", ...)` is immediately followed by :94 `Picker("Direction", selection:...)` with .pickerStyle(.segmented) (:101). On macOS a segmented Picker with a non-empty label string renders the label inline, producing "Flip" then "Direction  [Horizontal | Vertical]" — two labels for one concept.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Use `Picker("Flip direction", ...).labelsHidden()` and rely on the toggle as the heading, or drop the toggle label redundancy; either way set an .accessibilityLabel so VoiceOver still announces purpose.

findings_deduped.title: Sliders have no min/max endpoint labels for non-obvious ranges
findings_deduped.rule: HIG Sliders: when the range or units aren't self-evident, provide min/max value labels (or accessory text) so users understand the scale; a bare track from 0.1×–3.0× or -180°–180° gives no scale cue.
findings_deduped.evidence: Sliders declare ranges with no minimumValueLabel/maximumValueLabel: feather 0...30 (MaskFiltersForm.swift:36), threshold 0...1 (:56), scale 0.1...3.0 (TransformsForm.swift:35), rotate -180...180 (:79), blur 0...60 (BackgroundFiltersForm.swift:38), desaturate 0...1 (:58). Only the current value is shown.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Use the Slider(value:in:) initializer overload that takes `minimumValueLabel:` / `maximumValueLabel:` (e.g. Text("0") / Text("30 px")), a stock SwiftUI affordance.

findings_deduped.title: Disclosure header hit target is below the recommended minimum height
findings_deduped.rule: HIG / AppKit pointer & hit-target sizing: interactive rows should meet the comfortable minimum target; a ~24pt-tall control row is under the recommended ~28pt for reliable pointer/keyboard hit.
findings_deduped.evidence: ClickRowDisclosure.swift:24-25 sets `.contentShape(Rectangle())` then only `.padding(.vertical, 4)` around a `.headline` HStack; total row height is roughly headline cap height (~16pt) + 8pt = ~24pt. Width is full (Spacer), but height is short for a primary tap target.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Increase to .padding(.vertical, 6) (or set a .frame(minHeight: 28)) so the header row meets the comfortable target height; keep the full-width contentShape.

findings_deduped.title: Cutout thumbnail / Name icon are fixed 22×22 / inline glyphs — below HIG hit/target sizing if treated as actionable
findings_deduped.rule: HIG Accessibility: minimum hit target ~44×44 pt for actionable elements.
findings_deduped.evidence: FileListView.swift:264 `.frame(width: 22, height: 22)` cutout thumb and the in-cell tap text (271-277) form actionable surfaces well under 44pt. They are inside a table row, but the onTapGesture makes the 22pt thumb-adjacent text the only open trigger.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Once the in-cell onTapGesture is removed (see prior finding) these become purely decorative and the sizing concern disappears; keep them informational only.

findings_deduped.title: Empty-state overlay condition diverges from sorted/visible data driving the Table
findings_deduped.rule: Heuristic / charter "every number on screen comes from real state": the empty placeholder must reflect the same set the Table renders.
findings_deduped.evidence: FileListView.swift:84 `.overlay { if viewModel.visibleFiles.isEmpty { emptyState } }` while the Table is fed `sortedFiles` = `viewModel.visibleFiles.sorted(...)` (162-164). These share the same source so they agree today, but the empty overlay sits on top of an already-rendered (empty) Table rather than replacing it, so the column headers remain visible behind "Drop images here" — Finder hides headers in its empty state.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Gate the whole Table vs emptyState with an `if`/`else` so column headers don't show behind the empty placeholder, matching Finder's empty-folder presentation.

findings_deduped.title: Empty-state Try Demo button risks baking in sample data the user could mistake for their work
findings_deduped.rule: Charter NO FAKE DATA: "first-launch state is empty — the drop zone, nothing else"; "don't bake in sample/demo files ... anywhere the user might mistake them for their own work."
findings_deduped.evidence: FileListView.swift:152-154 empty state shows a "Try Demo" Button calling `viewModel.startBuiltInDemo()`. The design SSOT empty state (app.jsx:451-456) shows only "Drop a folder or images here / or use Add files…" — no demo button. If startBuiltInDemo seeds bundled images into the queue they appear indistinguishable from user files, which the charter forbids.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Confirm startBuiltInDemo only opens documentation/sample in a clearly-labeled sandbox, or remove the button to match the SSOT empty state (drop zone + Add files only).

findings_deduped.title: Context menu 'Add files…' is a permanently-disabled no-op placeholder
findings_deduped.rule: Charter NO FAKE UI: "no aspirational labels"; HIG context menus: don't show disabled commands that do nothing.
findings_deduped.evidence: FileListView.swift:185-186 `if ids.isEmpty { Button("Add files…", action: { /* handled via toolbar */ }).disabled(true) }` — an always-disabled menu item with an empty action that exists only as a label.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Either wire the empty-selection context menu "Add files…" to the real file importer used by the toolbar, or omit the item entirely (an empty-selection right-click can show no menu).

findings_deduped.title: Sort comparator for missing dimensions/bytes sorts incorrectly relative to spec ('—' rows)
findings_deduped.rule: HIG Lists and tables: sorting must be predictable; SSOT shows real dims per row. Charter: numbers reflect real state.
findings_deduped.evidence: FileListView.swift:343-344 `bytesSortKey = bytes ?? -1` and `pixelArea = (width ?? 0) * (height ?? 0)`. Files lacking metadata (rendered as "—", sizeText/dimsText 173-181) sort as if size=-1 / area=0, intermixing unknown rows with genuine small files rather than grouping them. Default sortOrder (9-11) is by name ascending which is fine, but numeric sorts mislead.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Sort unknown-metadata rows to a consistent end of the list (e.g. via a comparator that orders nil last) so '—' rows don't masquerade as the smallest real files.

findings_deduped.title: Title and message duplicate the same fact; message is redundant with title
findings_deduped.rule: HIG Alerts: the title should be a short, complete-sentence question or statement; the message should add new information, not restate the title. SSOT drift: copy is not specified in the design (no modal copy exists in app.jsx/data.jsx), so copy must follow HIG cleanly.
findings_deduped.evidence: FileListView.swift:94 title 'Remove N images from queue?' and line 104 message 'They will be removed from the queue. Files on disk are not affected.' — first sentence of the message restates the title; only 'Files on disk are not affected' is new.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Trim the message to the only novel, reassuring fact: `Text("Files on disk are not affected.")`. Keep the title as the question.

findings_deduped.title: Confirm button label redundantly repeats the count already in the title
findings_deduped.rule: HIG Alerts/Buttons: button titles should be short verb phrases describing the action (e.g. 'Remove', 'Delete'); the count belongs in the title, not echoed in the button. Stock macOS alerts use a concise verb on the action button.
findings_deduped.evidence: FileListView.swift:94 title already says 'Remove \(pendingDeletionIDs.count) images', and FileListView.swift:98 button repeats it: `Button("Remove \(pendingDeletionIDs.count) from Queue", role: .destructive)`.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Shorten the destructive button to `Button("Remove", role: .destructive)` (or 'Remove from Queue'); the count is carried by the title.

findings_deduped.title: Empty-selection guard in handleDelete is correct but the dialog can present a stale/zero count title
findings_deduped.rule: HIG Alerts: alert text must reflect real state (charter 'every number on screen comes from real state'). The title interpolates pendingDeletionIDs.count, which is only set inside the >=10 branch; the binding reset paths leave room for a 0 flash if re-presented.
findings_deduped.evidence: FileListView.swift:94 title uses `pendingDeletionIDs.count`; FileListView.swift:100 and 102 reset `pendingDeletionIDs = []` on both actions. Title/message are evaluated against the live binding, so a re-trigger before set could render 'Remove 0 images'.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Snapshot the count into a dedicated @State Int set at trigger time and render the dialog copy from that snapshot, or assert count>0 before flipping showDeleteConfirm (already guarded) and avoid resetting to [] until the dialog fully dismisses.

findings_deduped.title: Filename token chips ({name} {ext} {n:02}) are custom-painted pill buttons rather than stock controls
findings_deduped.rule: Charter: 'Custom views are for composing app-specific content, never for repainting OS chrome / button shapes.' Stock chips would be Button with .bordered/.borderedProminent and .controlSize(.small), inheriting system styling.
findings_deduped.evidence: Screenshot shows three rounded grey pills '{name}', '{ext}', '{n:02}' below the title. design/project/app.jsx:384-386 styles them as className='token' custom buttons; they read as hand-styled chips, not stock macOS buttons.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Render as Button('{name}') { ... }.buttonStyle(.bordered).controlSize(.small) so they inherit system corner radius, hover, and focus ring instead of a custom pill.

findings_deduped.title: Mixed control idiom: feather/threshold use Slider, expand/contract use Stepper, inconsistent within one section
findings_deduped.rule: HIG (Controls / Consistency): use a consistent control type for analogous numeric inputs in the same group so users build one mental model. macOS pixel-amount adjustments are typically a single control type per group.
findings_deduped.evidence: Sources/Views/Settings/MaskFiltersForm.swift: featherRow (line 33) and thresholdRow (line 53) use Slider with a trailing 'N px' readout, while expandRow (line 71) and contractRow (line 86) use Stepper('Expand: N px'). In this screenshot the checked feather row shows a slider + '8 px'; the (collapsed) Expand/Contract rows would instead reveal steppers — inconsistent affordance for the same 'mask refinement, px amount' task.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Pick one idiom for all four px controls in 'Mask refinement' (e.g. Slider + monospaced readout, or Stepper) so the section is internally consistent.

findings_deduped.surface: Inspector / Config panel — subtitle and footer text
findings_deduped.title: Developer-facing copy ('Filters (--filter chain)', 'used when text alone is empty') uses CLI/implementation jargon instead of plain user language
findings_deduped.rule: Charter: 'No aspirational labels... every status string truthful and user-facing'; HIG (Writing): use clear, human language, not implementation details. The '--filter chain' flag and 'text alone is empty' are developer concepts.
findings_deduped.evidence: Screenshot shows the subtitle 'Filters (--filter chain)' under the title and footer 'Composed from GUI controls (used when text alone is empty)' (Sources/Views/Settings/AdvancedChainEditor.swift:51). These expose the CLI flag name and internal precedence logic to the end user.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Reword to user terms, e.g. drop the '--filter chain' flag reference and say 'Adjustments'; replace the footer with plain text describing precedence in user words, or remove it if the advanced field is hidden by default.

findings_deduped.title: Inspector toggle and Add Files use icon+title in toolbar but the Run/Stop button is title-only — inconsistent toolbar item presentation
findings_deduped.rule: HIG (macOS toolbars): keep toolbar items visually consistent; if items use symbols, all action items should carry a representative symbol so they read as a coherent set, and labels should be available consistently.
findings_deduped.evidence: BgBgOneApp.swift:187 Button("Add Files…", systemImage: "plus") and :209-211 Button(..., systemImage: "sidebar.right") both have symbols, but the central Run all/Stop button (:195) has no systemImage — mixed icon/no-icon items in one toolbar.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Give the process button a symbol (e.g. systemImage: viewModel.activeRun != nil ? "stop.fill" : "play.fill") so all three toolbar items are symbol+label consistent, or make all label-only.

findings_deduped.title: Run all/Stop toggle uses a label swap with no distinct destructive/stop affordance
findings_deduped.rule: HIG (controls/feedback): a toggle that switches into a 'Stop' state should give clear visual feedback distinguishing the running state (e.g. a stop symbol or de-emphasized prominence); a plain text swap on a .borderedProminent button can read as the same affordance.
findings_deduped.evidence: BgBgOneApp.swift:195-206: the same .borderedProminent style is used for both "Run all" and "Stop"; only the title text differs. No symbol or role change signals the active/stop state beyond the word.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: When activeRun != nil, switch the button to systemImage "stop.fill" and consider .tint(.red) or a less-prominent style so the running/stop state is visually distinct from the idle Run all state.

findings_deduped.title: Process toolbar button lacks a keyboard shortcut despite being the primary action
findings_deduped.rule: HIG (keyboard): the most important/primary action should be keyboard-reachable with a standard shortcut; Add Files… has ⌘O (via menu) but the primary process action has no shortcut.
findings_deduped.evidence: BgBgOneApp.swift:195-206 Run all/Stop button defines no .keyboardShortcut, and BgBgOneCommands (:31-67) has no menu entry for Run/Stop either, so the primary action is mouse-only.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Add .keyboardShortcut(.return, modifiers: .command) (or similar) to the process button and/or expose a Run All / Stop menu command in BgBgOneCommands so it is keyboard-reachable.

findings_deduped.title: brew-command 'code' chip is custom-painted with a hardcoded fill instead of a stock container
findings_deduped.rule: Charter: 'Standard SwiftUI primitives only — no custom-painted OS chrome'; system materials for surfaces (CLAUDE.md:64-66, :28).
findings_deduped.evidence: MissingBinaryView.swift:29-31 .background(DesignColor.bgSoft, in: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius:6)) where bgSoft is hardcoded #f3f4f6 (DesignTokens.swift:15). A fixed light fill won't adapt and re-skins a code field by hand.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Use .background(.quaternary, in: .rect(cornerRadius:6)) or .regularMaterial; better, drop the brew chip entirely per the lying-label finding.

findings_deduped.title: Charter says MissingBinaryView 'disables actions' but the view's only stateful action (Retry) is always enabled with no disabled-state handling
findings_deduped.rule: Charter NO FALLBACKS: 'the app shows MissingBinaryView and disables actions' (CLAUDE.md:49, :81).
findings_deduped.evidence: MissingBinaryView.swift:43 Button("Retry", action: onRetry) is unconditionally enabled; the surface's mandated INTERACTION 'disabled actions' is not represented anywhere in this view (there is no disabled processing/primary action shown to demonstrate the app's actions are disabled). The disabling presumably lives in the parent, but this surface shows no evidence of it.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: This is correct only if the parent swaps the entire content area for MissingBinaryView (no toolbar process action reachable). Verify in WindowChrome/AppViewModel that toolbar 'Remove background' is .disabled while in missingBinary state; add a source-scan asserting the primary process action is guarded by the missing-binary state.

findings_deduped.title: Decorative glyph not hidden from VoiceOver and title is not exposed as a heading
findings_deduped.rule: HIG Accessibility: decorative images should be hidden from assistive tech; primary screen title should carry a heading trait for navigation.
findings_deduped.evidence: MissingBinaryView.swift:12 Image(systemName: "questionmark.app.dashed") has no .accessibilityHidden(true); Text("Where's bgbgone?") :16 has no .accessibilityAddTraits(.isHeader).
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Add .accessibilityHidden(true) to the decorative SF Symbol and .accessibilityAddTraits(.isHeader) to the title Text.

findings_deduped.title: Run all / Stop toolbar button uses no systemImage, breaking title-bar visual parity with the other toolbar items
findings_deduped.rule: Charter "Finder eyeball test" + HIG Toolbars: toolbar items should present consistently (Finder's primary actions are labeled icon buttons). The other two items here use systemImage; this one is text-only prominent.
findings_deduped.evidence: BgBgOneApp.swift:195 `Button(viewModel.activeRun != nil ? "Stop" : "Run all") { ... }.buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)` — no systemImage, unlike Add Files… (:187 systemImage:"plus") and the inspector toggle (:209 systemImage:"sidebar.right").
findings_deduped.fixSketch: This is a deliberate primary-action prominence choice (matches design's "Remove background from N" prominent button) and is defensible; if parity is desired, add systemImage:"wand.and.stars"/"stop.fill". Keep .borderedProminent. Low severity — note, not blocker.

findings_deduped.title: Window title set twice (WindowGroup label + navigationTitle), risking redundant/inconsistent title-bar text
findings_deduped.rule: HIG Windows: "You typically display the title of a macOS window in the title bar" — one authoritative title. The charter wants real title text `bgbgone` in the real title bar.
findings_deduped.evidence: BgBgOneApp.swift:18 `WindowGroup("bgbgone")` sets the scene/window title; BgBgOneApp.swift:144 `.navigationTitle("bgbgone")` sets it again on the detail. On macOS the navigationTitle inside NavigationSplitView wins for the title bar, so the WindowGroup string is effectively dead but is what shows in the Window menu / app switcher.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Acceptable as-is (both resolve to "bgbgone"), but to remove the double source of truth, keep `.navigationTitle("bgbgone")` (it pairs with navigationSubtitle) and use a non-titling WindowGroup id, or document that the WindowGroup label only feeds the Window menu. No functional bug today; guard with a source-scan that both strings stay equal.

findings_deduped.title: navigationSubtitle blanked to empty string on first launch instead of conveying window state
findings_deduped.rule: HIG Windows: "Use the title area to describe the current screen if it provides useful context ... helps people confirm their location." The subtitle helper already computes a useful empty-state string but it is suppressed.
findings_deduped.evidence: BgBgOneApp.swift:145 `.navigationSubtitle(viewModel.files.isEmpty ? "" : subtitle)` forces empty when no files, even though the `subtitle` computed property (:219-223) returns "Drop a folder to begin" for the n==0 case — that branch is unreachable.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Either use `.navigationSubtitle(subtitle)` unconditionally (so first launch reads "Drop a folder to begin"), or delete the now-dead n==0 branch in `subtitle`. Pick one and make them consistent.

findings_deduped.title: DesignRadius.window = 14 (window corner radius) exists as a token that, if applied, would conflict with real NSWindow chrome
findings_deduped.rule: Charter "NO FAKE CHROME": real NSWindow chrome only; the OS owns the window corner radius. A 14pt window radius is a custom-frame smell.
findings_deduped.evidence: Sources/Views/DesignTokens.swift:33 `static let window: CGFloat = 14` mirrors styles.css:31 `--radius-window: 14px`. The real NSWindow already supplies the system corner radius; any view applying DesignRadius.window at window level would paint a fake frame inside the real one.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Remove DesignRadius.window (it has no legitimate use in a real-chrome app) or assert via source-scan that it is never used. Keep regular/small radii for in-content cards only.

findings_deduped.title: windowResizability(.contentMinSize) diverges from charter's documented .contentSize example
findings_deduped.rule: Charter Tech baseline: "WindowGroup + .windowResizability(.contentSize)". HIG Windows: non-resizable windows feel broken on Mac — windows should be freely resizable.
findings_deduped.evidence: BgBgOneApp.swift:22 `.windowResizability(.contentMinSize)` vs CLAUDE.md:124 which illustrates `.contentResizability(.contentSize)`. NOTE: .contentMinSize is actually the HIG-correct choice (lets the window grow past idealWidth/Height and be freely resized down to minWidth 1100 / minHeight 720 from BgBgOneApp.swift:20), whereas .contentSize would clamp the window to the content's size range. The code is arguably better than the charter example.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Keep .contentMinSize (correct for a resizable Finder-like window). Reconcile the charter wording to allow .contentMinSize, OR confirm intent. No functional fix needed; flagged only as a documented-vs-actual drift.

findings_deduped.title: Non-system typography: hardcoded point sizes and manual tracking imitating a type scale
findings_deduped.rule: Charter: system fonts (.system/.headline/...) at system sizes; "never a hand-rolled tracking/weight stack pretending to be SF Pro." HIG (Typography): prefer Dynamic Type / semantic text styles.
findings_deduped.evidence: Pervasive fixed sizes: `.font(.system(size: 12))` (50), `size: 11` (54,121,190), `size: 11.5` (81), `size: 10.5` (157,169), `size: 10` (217) plus manual letter-spacing SectionLabel DebugOverlay.swift:218 `.tracking(0.06 * 10)` on uppercased text — a hand-rolled cap-label scale rather than a semantic style.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Use semantic styles (`.caption`, `.caption2`, `.footnote`, `.body`) and drop manual `.tracking`. If kept DEBUG-only, lower priority. Source-scan test: no `.tracking(` and no raw `size:` font literals in shipping Views.

findings_deduped.surface: Dual preview / ORIGINAL & CUTOUT corner labels
findings_deduped.title: Corner caption contrast not guaranteed over arbitrary image / checkerboard
findings_deduped.rule: WCAG AA (4.5:1 for small text). A .thinMaterial capsule with semibold caption sits over the user's photo (ORIGINAL) and over the transparency checkerboard (CUTOUT); over light image content the translucent label can drop below AA.
findings_deduped.evidence: Sources/Views/Preview/BigDualPreview.swift:156-162 `cornerLabel` uses `.font(.caption.weight(.semibold).smallCaps())` with `.background(.thinMaterial, in: Capsule())` and no explicit foreground/stroke. Screenshot shows faint "ORIGINAL"/"CUTOUT" pills top-left of each pane that read low-contrast against the bright butterfly and the white checkerboard.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Use `.regularMaterial` (more opaque) instead of `.thinMaterial`, set `.foregroundStyle(.primary)`, and add a hairline `.overlay(Capsule().strokeBorder(.separator))` so the label keeps AA contrast regardless of underlying pixels.

findings_deduped.title: Dismiss control uses .tertiary foreground — weak contrast and small target
findings_deduped.rule: WCAG AA + HIG hit-target: a primary dismiss affordance rendered in .tertiary grey on a light banner risks failing 4.5:1, and a bare SF Symbol with no padding is a sub-minimum target.
findings_deduped.evidence: Sources/Views/FileListView.swift:317-321 the dismiss `Button` renders `Image(systemName:"xmark.circle.fill").foregroundStyle(.tertiary)` with `.buttonStyle(.plain)` and no frame/contentShape. In the screenshot the X at the right edge of the "Added 3 images from bgbgone-demo" toast is a faint grey glyph.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Use `.foregroundStyle(.secondary)` for adequate contrast and wrap the glyph in `.frame(width:28,height:28).contentShape(Rectangle())`; add `.accessibilityLabel("Dismiss")` and an accessibilityIdentifier.

findings_deduped.title: Mask-refinement rows use ad-hoc spacing (12/6/4 pt) unrelated to the DesignRadius scale
findings_deduped.rule: HIG (Layout & spacing): use a consistent spacing scale; charter implies tokenized geometry (DesignRadius 14/8/5). Mixed hard-coded paddings break visual rhythm.
findings_deduped.evidence: MaskFiltersForm.swift uses VStack spacing 12, .padding(.vertical, 6), and inner spacing 4; ClickRowDisclosure adds .padding(.vertical, 4) and .padding(.top, 4). These magic numbers are not derived from any spacing token and produce the slightly uneven gaps visible between the four checkboxes in the screenshot.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Introduce a DesignSpacing scale (or use Form/Section default spacing) and reference it instead of literals, or move these rows into a stock `Form { Section }` which supplies consistent system spacing.

findings_deduped.title: Disclosure header uses .help tooltip but rows give no inline explanation of destructive/aggressive mask edits
findings_deduped.rule: HIG (Controls / labels): controls that alter output should make their effect discoverable; charter "label clarity & truthfulness." Expand/Contract mask are dilation/erosion that can clip the subject, with no affordance signalling that.
findings_deduped.evidence: In the screenshot all four checkboxes are unchecked with terse labels ("Expand mask", "Contract mask"). The only explanation lives in a hover-only .help on the section header (MaskFiltersForm.swift:20). Erosion ("Contract mask") can destructively eat into the cutout edge yet is presented identically to the benign "Soften edges".
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Add per-row `.help(...)` and a one-line secondary caption under each Toggle (Text(...).font(.footnote).foregroundStyle(.secondary)) so the effect is visible without hovering.

findings_deduped.title: Debug overlay uses custom dark-filled button style and hardcoded colors, not stock SwiftUI
findings_deduped.rule: Charter (CLAUDE.md:64-73): stock SwiftUI primitives only; custom button shapes imitating bordered styles are forbidden; use system semantic colors. The Tweaks panel ('Reset to fresh state', 'Mark all done') uses `MiniDebugButtonStyle` drawing `RoundedRectangle.fill(Color(white:0.22))` with white text — a hand-rolled dark button, plus DesignColor.* hardcoded tokens throughout.
findings_deduped.evidence: Screenshot shows two near-black filled pill buttons in the Tweaks panel. DebugOverlay.swift:98-109 `.buttonStyle(MiniDebugButtonStyle())`, lines 232-239 fill `Color(white:0.22)` with `.foregroundStyle(.white)`. Note: this is a test/debug scaffold, not shipping chrome, hence low severity — but it should not paint custom OS-like controls and should be excluded from any shipping build.
findings_deduped.fixSketch: Replace MiniDebugButtonStyle with stock `.buttonStyle(.bordered)` / `.borderedProminent` and `.controlSize(.small)`; replace DesignColor.* with `.primary`/`.secondary`/`.tint`. Ensure the debug overlay is compiled out (`#if DEBUG`) so it never reaches the Finder-eyeball-tested shipping window.
